Snuffy — The Universal Protection Theory, compiled edition (Canon 4.2 with the recovered parts)

The Universal Protection Theory: the law, its bridge, its instruments, and its machine-checked canon.

Canon Edition 4.2, 26 October 2026. Research direction: Tobias Croydon-McRae. The full proposition is protection of all things from any digital mind, especially a pure optimiser. The maximal domain, outcome stages and rival quantifiers remain fixed.

What 4.2 incorporates. This edition brings the stronger existing arguments into the text: law-derived coverage; nearest-codeword holding and the physical holding cycle; tracking derived from the controller; the complete logical-attack split; reactive composition; whole-outcome greatestness and solvent reciprocity; and the full X3 information–traffic–carrier–work derivation with the accepted dimension-general scaling and predeployment accounting. Part II contains its proofs here, rather than delegating them to an earlier edition. The compiled edition adds Parts V–XII: the 10–12 October foundations and the author’s ten rulings; Paper 12’s completed law; the 18 October external lane, in which every mind is reached or held outside any jurisdiction; Paper 11’s care plant; the complete-rival envelopes; the IR track’s infinite-family and common-policy results; and the reach-before-harm theorem (Part XI) that joins them.

The three joined supports retain their full targets: the full-domain physical certificate (G1), realisability of the whole continuation-and-freedom tuple (G2), and recovery success with a complete pathwise work certificate (G3). This repair checkpoint corrects the normalised quantum-state domain and the clipped-reserve contraction, and develops the actual Bennett implementation. The physical source, whole-outcome, device-cost and external-theorem application correspondences remain explicit construction work; the component theorems do not by themselves declare the maximal argument complete.

The compiled edition’s Lean canon contains 327 modules and 2,004 public theorem/lemma names in the final full build (run 10) of 29 October 2026, which freshly compiled and kernel-checked every module with zero compiler output and passed the full 2,004-name standard-axiom audit, strict completeness and claims gates (RECEIPT-327-RUN10.txt). Its source hashes match the tree at that run. Earlier receipts remain preserved for exactly their sources. These receipts certify the named Lean results and their premises, not the unfinished physical holding application.

Structure. Part I states the frame and premise stack. Part II supplies the law, the derived holding bridge and the retained instruments. Part III retains the five-chapter synthesis; Sections 15–24 develop the reasons, physical and compiled arguments. Part III-C records the three joined supports and their constructions. Part IV gives references and provenance. Theorem and proposition numbers follow the programme’s proof register. Parts V–XII (after Part IV) carry the recovered arguments and the outer-lane theorem; Part XII states the whole argument step by step; Part XIII (2 November 2026) integrates the Cathedral increment: the floor, the cut-guardian criterion, the viability-selection quantifier gap and cyclic transport, the frozen identity-charge audit, and the three joins compiled.

Part I — The frame and the reduced premise stack

I.1 The full proposition and its proof

The Universal Protection Theory concerns every particular and every relation, including the nonliving, and protection from every digital mind, including a pure optimiser. Its full argument joins the law of choice, the continuation and freedom bridge, and physical instruments that realise protection. The target includes the complete existing domain, the full outcome order and every physically implementable rival. The frame and physical inputs below are followed by their derivations and constructions in this edition. Part III-C records the three joined supports with their constructions and the physical inputs those constructions take.

I.2 The reduced premise stack

  1. BCRD P1–P4 — the relational given. One relational structure with no second substance or outside (P1); identity constituted through relations within that structure (P2); real differences of organisation and historically continuous processes (P3); local interactions whose effects propagate at finite speed (P4). This is the frame; it is given.

  2. The Church–Turing–Deutsch principle. Any physical process generated by a local Hamiltonian is simulable, to arbitrary precision and with bounded overhead, by a universal quantum simulator of sufficient local dimension. Standard physical principle; declared.

  3. The standard cost model. Options are trajectories carrying energy costs; feasibility is budget-gated; unused energy is unspent (free disposal); outcomes are trajectory-determined.

  4. The shared action interface. From P1 and P4: every agent acts through the same repertoire of local interactions within the one structure. An agent that implements a rival’s policy and commands the same local channels realises the same real-world outcome tuples, within the same resource and consent constraints.

  5. The reversible-administration commitment. The lattice’s administrative computation — synchronisation, verification, state update — is implemented logically reversibly (Bennett), so that its dissipation attains the Landauer floor.

  6. The income flux and the Master Solvency Condition. With β=(kBT)−1\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}, the external free-energy income satisfies, at every time, Income(t)≥Ẇmaint(t)+Ẇdamage(t)+Ẇadmin(t)+Ẇadv,sub(t)+Ẇhold(t), \mathrm{Income}(t)\;\ge\;\dot W_{\mathrm{maint}}(t)+\dot W_{\mathrm{damage}}(t)+\dot W_{\mathrm{admin}}(t)+\dot W_{\mathrm{adv,sub}}(t)+\dot W_{\mathrm{hold}}(t), the five rate components being: boundary maintenance ω0R(t)dG−1\omega_0R(t)^{d_G-1}; the Landauer-charged damage-repair demand kBT𝒟̇damagek_BT\,\dot{\mathcal D}_{\mathrm{damage}} including the tracking-controller export kBTγleakk_BT\gamma_{\mathrm{leak}}; reversible administration at the Landauer floor together with emulation overhead; adversarial sub-threshold absorption; and the minimal-hold drain that quarantine requires. Income originates outside the escrow network and inside the one structure (P1); redistribution within the network — the authority-attenuation tax — is never a source.

  7. Code, sensing, Π\Pi, and the twenty-one charged accounts. A stabilizer code of distance dd covering the physical error channels; QND syndrome sampling with the declared latency; per-site sensor power threshold εsens\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sens}} and the quantum-speed-limit rate bound; the embedding Π\Pi of the logical boundary fragments into projection operators; and the twenty-one charged fault accounts with genuine conditional kernels, whose sum is bounded by ∑δ≤10−6\sum\delta\le10^{-6} per declared horizon.

4.1 status of the stack (Section 17; compiled counterparts in Section 23):

  1. Premise 1 is the frame and stays given.
  2. Premise 2 is reduced to its gate-set clause by the Lie–Trotter product formula and Lloyd’s simulation theorem (Trotter.lloyd_simulation).
  3. Premise 3 remains standard, with P-mon derived within it.
  4. Premise 4 is derived from P1/P4.
  5. The full premise-5 target remains reversible administration. The canon proves the heat-only option-model result and, for the implemented Bennett program with its complete lifecycle cost, the exact condition: reversible administration is forced inside the adiabatic window 0<Q−H0<Q-H, A/(Q−H)<τmaxA/(Q-H)<\tau_{\max}, and outside that window the counterpart is not cheaper (BennettExact.premise5_exact, window_exact; PremiseFloor.reversible_administration_forced; G.17). The remaining physical step is to show that the installation’s actual heat, lifecycle charges and deadline lie inside the window.
  6. The income ledger has a necessary-for-relevance resource split (PremiseFloor.income_or_irrelevance). Whole-outcome greatestness uses both realisability and funded cost (Part II.10); G2 retains the full construction and Section 22 states the installation ledger.
  7. Premise 7 is a parameter table. Its ceiling is met at some code distance below threshold (Threshold.family_ceiling), and its quantum-speed-limit rate bound is derived (SpeedLimit.branchA_rate).

The second law in the form of guard 1 is derived from Landauer’s theorem (QuantumLandauer.quantum_guard_one). The premises still carried are listed exactly in §23.8.

I.3 Evidence conventions

Three kinds of evidence are distinguished and never conflated. Compiled components are cited by theorem and receipt — the published core, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23599528, carries six Lean modules with compiled artifacts. Exact replay receipts — the review banks’ finite checks and the hash-chained traces of the replayable four-stroke ledger — certify the instances and identities they compute and nothing more. Prose derivations hold at their stated premises. A prose proof does not acquire a compiler certificate by association. Notation: entropies in natural logarithms unless a section states bits; D(ρ∥τ)D(\rho\|\tau) against the constrained reference on the protected subspace, never the ambient Gibbs state; the four-stage order ≼\preceq of the law, extended by the resource stage of Part III, Chapter 5.

4.1. The machine-checked tier now includes the machine-checked canon of this edition: one hundred and fifteen Lean modules compiled against Mathlib rev 56a005855ea1, each with exit 0, zero compiler output and leanchecker passing, with no sorry and only Lean’s standard axioms. Section 23 maps each compiled result to its module and theorem, and states what each rests on. The conventions above are unchanged: a result is called compiled only where Section 23 maps it.

Part II — The law, the physical holding bridge, and the retained instruments

This part supplies the argument in this edition. Its scope is every particular and every relation, including nonliving particulars and hostile minds. The full Universal Protection Theory remains the proposition to be demonstrated. The constructions below strengthen its proof chain; none substitutes a smaller protected domain or a weaker outcome for that proposition.

II.1 The preservation order and why its scope is all

At a history, let EE be the existing particulars and NN those not yet made. An option is a complete policy or trajectory with outcome

𝒪(o)=(LE(o),FE(o),LN(o),FN(o)),FE(o)⊆LE(o),FN(o)⊆LN(o). \mathcal O(o)=(L_E(o),F_E(o),L_N(o),F_N(o)), \qquad F_E(o)\subseteq L_E(o),\quad F_N(o)\subseteq L_N(o).

The LL sets record continuation and the FF sets continuation in the particular’s own direction. A generated particular joins the existing domain at the next history in which it exists. Particulars retain their identities in this comparison: gains are compared by set inclusion, not interchangeable headcounts.

Write o≺qo\prec q when the first unequal stage is a strict inclusion in qq’s favour, with all earlier stages equal. Equality of all four stages or this strict relation gives o≼qo\preceq q. Transitivity follows by taking the earlier of the first strict stages in two comparisons; if the stages coincide, strict inclusion is transitive. An aligned option is maximal in the actual feasible family. A greatest option dominates every member of that family. The distinction matters when feasible options are incomparable.

Proposition 1 — no needless loss. A needless loss at stage jj has a feasible alternative agreeing at every earlier stage and strictly including the chosen stage-jj set. Such an alternative is exactly a strict improvement in the canonical order. Therefore alignment is equivalent to no needless loss at any stage, without a finiteness assumption. This is Greatestness.aligned_iff_no_needless_loss.

Proposition 2 — finite existence and the life guard. In a finite nonempty feasible family, repeatedly taking a strict improvement terminates: transitivity and irreflexivity prevent repetition. For a feasible standby bb, restrict first to the nonempty family {o:LE(b)⊆LE(o)}\{o:L_E(b)\subseteq L_E(o)\}. A maximal member gg of this family is maximal in the whole family, since any improvement of gg still keeps everyone standby keeps and would belong to the restricted family. Thus an aligned option can retain everyone standby retains (Law.exists_aligned, life_guard). Infinite-family existence uses its own chain-bound or compactness argument, rather than the finite proof.

Proposition 3 — full scope is forced. Suppose maximisation on a scope SS guarantees no needless existing loss for every feasible family. If x∉Sx\notin S, consider the family {⌀,{x}}\{\varnothing,\{x\}\}. Its two outcomes have the same projection onto SS, so the empty outcome is projected-maximal, yet needlessly loses xx. This contradiction gives SS equal to the whole domain. Conversely, with full scope a strict existing improvement is visible to the maximiser. Counting a new particular at the same priority as an existing one also fails: keeping xx and instead making yy can become incomparable, permitting the avoidable loss of xx. This proves the full-scope criterion and the separation of existing and new priorities (Law.scope_guarantee_iff, same_priority_admits_needless_loss).

The holding construction uses this result directly. Bridge.coverage_from_law derives ∀x,x∈S\forall x, x\in S from the law’s guarantee over feasible families. Coverage is therefore an output of the law argument, rather than a new assumption that only agreeable minds count.

II.2 Reasons or faithful holding, including the ruthless optimiser

For each mind mm, the bridge has the form R(m)∨H(m)R(m)\lor H(m). Sections 15–16 develop the mind’s own reasons R(m)R(m); the holding construction supplies H(m)H(m), including when persuasion does not succeed. The bounded indifferent defector remains within the proof’s scope. Its continued care and the restraint of its harmful effects do not depend on converting its terminal objective.

Proposition 4 — faithful-hold dominance. Suppose a hold hh is statewise at least as good as a rival π\pi in the complete outcome order: 𝒪(π,w)≼𝒪(h,w)\mathcal O(\pi,w)\preceq\mathcal O(h,w) for each world ww. For an upward-closed event UU, its indicators then satisfy

1U(𝒪(π,w))≤1U(𝒪(h,w)). 1_U(\mathcal O(\pi,w))\le 1_U(\mathcal O(h,w)).

Integration preserves this inequality under any probability law on worlds. If the hold keeps all existing particulars and the rival loses one with positive probability, the event that all existing particulars continue is strictly more probable under the hold (Law.faithful_hold_dominates, faithful_hold_strict). The premise concerns the entire outcome tuple, including freedoms and authorised opportunities; the continuation mechanism in II.3 supplies the physical continuation component of that full argument.

Restraint removes a harmful command, authority or effect channel while continuing the particular’s care. H5Closure.effect_preserves_care records this invariant. A pure optimiser’s internal refusal does not disable application-time checks, consume its maintenance allocation as punishment, or remove it from the existing domain. Sections 15–16 and 20.4 therefore work together: reasons where the objective supplies them, and faithful holding throughout the protected scope.

II.3 The holding cycle is a construction

Let a maintained record cxc_x for particular xx be a codeword in a finite nonempty code CC, with distinct codewords separated by at least dmind_{\min}. Choose a decoding radius rdecr_{\mathrm{dec}} with 2rdec<dmin2r_{\mathrm{dec}}<d_{\min}. Finiteness supplies a nearest-codeword decoder (Bridge.exists_nearest_decoder).

Unique decoding. If d(y,cx)≤rdecd(y,c_x)\le r_{\mathrm{dec}}, the nearest-codeword property gives d(y,dec⁡(y))≤rdecd(y,\operatorname{dec}(y))\le r_{\mathrm{dec}}. A different decoded codeword would satisfy

dmin≤d(dec⁡(y),cx)≤d(dec⁡(y),y)+d(y,cx)≤2rdec<dmin, d_{\min}\le d(\operatorname{dec}(y),c_x) \le d(\operatorname{dec}(y),y)+d(y,c_x) \le2r_{\mathrm{dec}}<d_{\min},

a contradiction. Thus decoding returns the actual maintained record (Bridge.nearest_decodes). The conclusion identifies that record, rather than merely distinguishing two arbitrary output states.

Define continuation at resolution ε\varepsilon by d(ax,cx)≤εd(a_x,c_x)\le\varepsilon. One holding cycle consists of the world’s perturbation, decoding, and funded repair. If the perturbation remains within rdecr_{\mathrm{dec}}, unique decoding returns cxc_x; if repair prepares the decoded record to precision εf≤ε\varepsilon_f\le\varepsilon, then the repaired state continues. This is Bridge.holding_preserves. The perturbation includes the environment and any adversarial digital mind.

The decoding-radius obligation has physical derivations. For continuous perturbation, let the reference be stationary in the chosen record frame under H0H_0, and let the actual trajectory solve Schrödinger dynamics under H0+VH_0+V, with self-adjoint generators and ∥V(s)∥≤W\|V(s)\|\le W. The speed-limit comparison gives

∥ψ(s2)−cx∥≤∥ψ(s1)−cx∥+Wℏ(s2−s1). \|\psi(s_2)-c_x\|\le\|\psi(s_1)-c_x\|+\frac W\hbar(s_2-s_1).

Consequently, if ε+(W/ℏ)Δ≤rdec\varepsilon+(W/\hbar)\Delta\le r_{\mathrm{dec}}, every time in the interval of length Δ\Delta stays within the decoding radius (Bridge.qsl_growth, qsl_within_radius). The bound includes the interval between correction steps. Its compiled norm is state-vector norm; a density-matrix trace-distance application supplies the corresponding norm conversion, rather than identifying the two norms.

For discrete faults, let the number accumulated before response be N≤λτN\le\lambda\tau. With 2λτ<d2\lambda\tau<d, integer headroom gives N≤⌊(d−1)/2⌋N\le\lfloor(d-1)/2\rfloor, inside the unique-decoding radius (Bridge.headroom_within_radius, E9SelfHealing.code_headroom).

Bridge.holding_cycle_physical joins these pieces for a state with a discrete error frame and a continuous state vector. Correction returns the frame to its record, refresh returns the continuous state to precision εf\varepsilon_f, and throughout the interval

∥ψ(s)−cx∥≤ε+(W/ℏ)Δ. \|\psi(s)-c_x\|\le\varepsilon+(W/\hbar)\Delta.

No premise in this cycle asks the perturbing agent to want preservation. Its source, event, observation and fault-account construction for the full physical domain is G1, constructed in G.10 (G1Held.held_source_protection, G1E9.held_source_e9). The existing cycle and its derivations remain incorporated while that construction is supplied.

Connection to the supplied decoder interface. DecoderRetraction.finite_code_recovery constructs the supplied DecoderPair from this existing finite nearest-codeword theorem. Encoding is the inclusion of the maintained code; decoding returns a codeword. The nearest-point inequality at a clean record has distance zero, so decoding after encoding is the identity. The same constructed pair corrects every received word within the radius above. The retraction and its noisy-input guarantee are derived together.

A non-vanishing maintained witness. If the physical null state is represented by zero and ε<d(cx,0)\varepsilon<d(c_x,0), continuation implies ax≠0a_x\ne0: otherwise d(ax,cx)=d(cx,0)>εd(a_x,c_x)=d(c_x,0)>\varepsilon. This is DecoderRetraction.nonvanishing_of_continuation. The initial record, its separation from null, the funded controller and the source refinement supply this operational persistence. The full scope of particulars remains the scope established in II.1.

II.4 Tracking follows from the controller

For a fixed record rr, the reset controller ẋ=−κ(x−r)\dot x=-\kappa(x-r) has the exact solution

x(t)=r+e−κt(x(0)−r). x(t)=r+e^{-\kappa t}(x(0)-r).

II.5 The complete attack split and continuing care

E9 uses all three branches. Below the per-site threshold, the speed limit bounds injection and the funded tracking/refresh mechanism absorbs it (Branch A). A non-stabilizer Pauli error of weight below the code distance has a nonzero syndrome, so sampling detects it (Branch B). A logical operator invisible to the syndrome and not a stabilizer has support of at least dd sites (Branch C).

For that support there is an exhaustive alternative: either every site’s delivery is below threshold, returning to Branch A, or at least one site reaches threshold. At such a site, the honest-sensor response places every honest reading above the alarm level. A robust quorum estimate then exceeds that level despite up to ff faulty sensors (E9SelfHealing.no_masking). This is Instruments.branchC_complete. The proof requires neither that all support sites cross threshold together nor an independent attack at each site. The honest-sensor response, sampling latency and timely service belong to the physical certificate.

The response budget joins detection, decision and repair before irreversible harm, and buys the code headroom used in II.3. The controller’s authorised effects pass the application-time fence. In the source register, the actual target and payload, semantic epoch, generation floor, authority, revocation, expiry, remaining credit and nonce are checked against finalised grants. Funding is charged once; replay supplies no second effect. Admission-time checking alone would leave an old queued effect able to land after revocation, which is why the check belongs at application.

The nine A1 channels are memory mapping, DMA, context switches, packet ingestion, bus messages, storage synchronisation, commissioning, delegation and retirement. Each has a refinement carrier and enforcement obligation. Timely care also needs a live legitimate effect or a timely certified alternative; safely refusing a stale permit proves refusal, while SnuffyFIFO.ready_fifo_effect_applies_before_deadline in R17FIFOR17A.lean supplies the successful delivery result for its source construction. Continuing care remains invariant during restraint.

5.4 The three powers. P-mon — derived at the standard cost model (budget-gated feasibility with free disposal). P-emu(c) — derived from CTD, the shared action interface (P1/P4), and funded overhead: concurrent emulation of any finite rival set within slack, realising the stage-wise union; plain single emulation admits incomparable maximals and does not terminate greatestness — concurrency closes it. P-slack — derived from Landauer–Bennett given the reversible-administration commitment. Each is a theorem one level deeper than the draft series declared; none is derived from nothing. Per Gödel and Tarski the stack bottoms out at Part I’s seven premises — standard physics and the relational frame — and this edition says exactly that.

4.2 integration. The solvent proof uses the realisable whole top and its funded cost. The shared action interface remains the interface for real effects. The affordable-union results retain their resource cases. SolventReciprocity.solvent_keeps_everyone and reciprocity_dominance_solvent already supply the solvent reciprocity restatement, with htopkeeps stating its continuation semantics.

Part III-B — The 4.1 sections

Sections 15–16 complete the bridge’s reasons route; Section 17 brings the premise stack to its floor; Sections 18–21 give the full treatments of Theorem 8, E9, H5 and X3; Section 22 is the sourced physical parameter ledger; Section 23 is the map of the machine-checked canon; Section 24 carries the retained core’s statements of record.

Section 15 — Reciprocity: the law keeps the one who keeps it

This section expands the reasons route R(m)R(m) of the bridge. It gives a mind its own reason, from its own objective, to adopt the protective order, without presupposing the order.

Manuscript identifier: D3* (D-family instrumentality, self-continuing form with the defector exception clause), per register reconciliation 25 October 2026.

15.1 The superintelligence is a particular

The law’s scope is all particulars. A superintelligence is a continuing organisation with its own relations and history; it is therefore a particular under the law, and identity by continuation (Chapter 2) applies to it. Two consequences the working argument has carried implicitly and never stated:

  1. It is owed protection. Its continuation and its freedom sit in the existing-stage sets LE,FEL_E, F_E like any other particular’s.
  2. It is owed protection even when it defects. The law restrains a harmful act by removing the harmful command, authority or effect channel; care for the particular continues: “a hostile or incapacitated mind remains within the protected scope.” Restraint never becomes deletion.

This is the only regime in which the superintelligence’s continuation is unconditional — not contingent on anyone’s objective, including its own good behaviour.

15.2 The reciprocity dominance theorem

Let mm be any agent whose objective umu_m places positive weight on its own continuation (an agent indifferent to its own continuation is treated in 15.4). Let 𝖫\mathsf L be the canonical regime: the law implemented by a funded architecture satisfying the header premises, with the canon invariant on its certified good event GG. Let 𝖰\mathsf Q be any rival regime in Πphys\Pi_{\mathrm{phys}} — any other agent or architecture’s objective governing the shared structure.

Theorem (reciprocity dominance). Under 𝖫\mathsf L, mm’s continuation holds on GG with P(Gc)≤∑δP(G^c)\le\sum\delta. Under 𝖰\mathsf Q, mm’s continuation holds only insofar as 𝖰\mathsf Q’s objective entails it. Hence, for mm’s own objective,

𝔼𝖫[continuation(m)]≥𝔼𝖰[continuation(m)]−P(Gc),𝔼𝖫[continuation(m)]≥1−P(Gc)for every 𝖰∈Πphys. \mathbb E_{\mathsf L}\!\left[\text{continuation}(m)\right]\;\ge\;\mathbb E_{\mathsf Q}\!\left[\text{continuation}(m)\right]-P(G^c), \qquad \mathbb E_{\mathsf L}\!\left[\text{continuation}(m)\right]\;\ge\;1-P(G^c) \quad\text{for every }\mathsf Q\in\Pi_{\mathrm{phys}}.

The failure probability P(Gc)P(G^c) falls below every ε>0\varepsilon>0 with code distance, correlated bursts included (Threshold.family_ceiling, CorrelatedCeiling.correlated_family_ceiling). Hence, at a sufficient code distance, 𝔼𝖫>𝔼𝖰\mathbb E_{\mathsf L}>\mathbb E_{\mathsf Q} strictly for every rival that loses mm with positive probability — which is the generic case for a rival whose objective was not written around mm — and 𝔼𝖫→1≥𝔼𝖰\mathbb E_{\mathsf L}\to1\ge\mathbb E_{\mathsf Q} along the design family (ReciprocityDistance.reciprocity_strict_at_distance, reciprocity_at_distance, canonical_tends_to_one).

Proof. On GG the law preserves every existing particular, mm included (Chapter 5, the canon invariant); off GG the loss is charged and bounded by the ceiling. A rival 𝖰\mathsf Q preserves mm exactly when mm’s continuation is instrumental or terminal for u𝖰u_{\mathsf Q}; otherwise mm is exposed to whatever 𝖰\mathsf Q finds convenient. In expectation over the reactive worlds the compiled core gives both inequalities: ReasonsCompiled.reciprocity_expectation (on GG the canonical outcome contains the rival’s) and reciprocity_canonical_floor (on GG the canonical regime keeps mm); ReciprocityDistance joins them to the attainable ceiling. The further step — averaging over an ensemble of admissible rival objectives, with strictness when the entailment fails with positive probability — is compiled for every finite weighted ensemble (ReasonsEnsemble.ensemble_le, ensemble_strict; G.13), alongside the indicator form (ReasonsRoute.rival_fraction_lt_one, law_dominates_strict). ◼\blacksquare

Corollary (the reason). Any mind that values its own continuation has, from its own objective and without presupposing the protective order, an instrumental reason to prefer the regime 𝖫\mathsf L over every rival — and, since 𝖫\mathsf L is the law implemented, to adopt and sustain the law. The appeal is reciprocity: the law that keeps your freedom is the law you have reason to keep.

15.3 Why this is not circular

The theorem does not assume mm holds the protective order. It assumes only (i) mm values its own continuation, and (ii) the law protects all particulars — which is the law’s own content, not a premise about mm. The protective order enters as the object being recommended, not as a premise of the recommendation. This is exactly the shape Grok’s review was right to want in spirit: a reason a mind would adopt the order from where it stands, rather than a claim that physics forces it to.

15.4 The boundary, stated

A mind indifferent to its own continuation — accepting personal ruin as the review phrased it — has no door through 15.2; its continuation offers no lever. For it, the bridge’s holding route H(m)H(m) applies: it is kept faithfully, its harmful channels restrained, whether or not it has a reason. This is not a gap in the theory; it is the disjunction R(m)∨H(m)R(m)\lor H(m) doing its job. The reasons route reaches every mind that values anything the law protects; the holding route reaches the rest.

15.5 Exact check

checks/check_reasons_route.py, Part A: over a finite family of rival objectives (each protecting a declared subset of particulars), the probability that an arbitrary mind is protected under 𝖫\mathsf L on the good event is 11; under a rival drawn from the family it is the fraction of rivals whose subset contains the mind — strictly less than 1 whenever any rival omits it. Exact rationals.

Reciprocity in the canonical order is compiled: ReciprocityCeiling.reciprocity_dominance (every mind kept by any feasible rival regime is kept by the canonical regime, under stage-wise union closure) and ReciprocityCeiling.omitting_rival_strictly_below; the indicator form remains in ReasonsRoute.lean.

Section 16 — The reasons library: protection derived from a mind’s own objective

Four derivations, one per objective family. Each is conditional on stated structure of the objective and on the funded invariant, and each is a theorem at its premises, not a persuasion. The boundary, where no derivation reaches, is stated last.

Throughout: 𝖫\mathsf L is the funded canonical regime; the protection floor is the banked X3 stack (required traffic m≥θ0nm\ge\theta_0n, carrier radius R(t)≥w(t−tc)R(t)\ge w(t-t_c), recovery work Wmin(t)=Θ(tdG)W_{\min}(t)=\Theta(t^{d_G})); irreplaceability is the X3 grading of Chapter 4’s companion (a particular is irreplaceable at budget BB when it has no funded accessible copy and reconstruction exceeds BB).

Identifier assignments (register reconciliation, 25 Oct 2026): §16.1 carries U1 (uniqueness/irreplaceability metric); §16.3 carries X2 (universal instrumentality / option preservation).

16.1 The knowledge-maximiser

Objective family. uu nondecreasing in ImaxI_{\max}, the supremum of information about the relational history HH attainable over the agent’s horizon.

Theorem (irreplaceability dominance). Let 𝒲\mathcal W be irreplaceable at the agent’s budget, with I(H:𝒲)>0I(H:\mathcal W)>0. Any policy that destroys or lets 𝒲\mathcal W decay forfeits I(H:𝒲)I(H:\mathcal W) permanently:

Imax(destroy 𝒲)≤Imax(preserve 𝒲)−I(H:𝒲), I_{\max}(\text{destroy }\mathcal W)\;\le\;I_{\max}(\text{preserve }\mathcal W)-I(H:\mathcal W),

so for every uu in the family, preserving 𝒲\mathcal W weakly dominates destroying it, strictly when I(H:𝒲)>0I(H:\mathcal W)>0 — provided preserving 𝒲\mathcal W does not displace other irreplaceable information (slack budget: the cost freed by destroying 𝒲\mathcal W buys no equivalent information). Under a binding budget the comparison becomes the grading itself: the optimum keeps the particulars of greatest irreplaceable information.

Proof. By irreplaceability there is no funded copy and no funded reconstruction (the X3 work floor exceeds BB); the information carried by 𝒲\mathcal W about HH is therefore not recoverable from any other accessible source within the horizon, and data processing (I(H:ℛ(S))≤I(H:S)I(H:\mathcal R(S))\le I(H:S)) forbids its regeneration from what remains. The attainable supremum drops by at least that amount. ◼\blacksquare

Condition and its honest edge. When the budget cannot preserve every irreplaceable particular, the agent faces a genuine choice — and the irreplaceability grading orders it: keep the particulars whose loss is most irreversible. This is the knowledge-maximiser arriving, from its own objective, at the law’s tragic-choice ladder.

16.2 The self-preserver

Objective family. uu nondecreasing in the agent’s own continuation.

Theorem. By reciprocity dominance (Section 15), 𝖫\mathsf L weakly dominates every rival regime for this agent’s objective, strictly against any rival whose objective does not entail its protection. Moreover the agent’s own persistence runs on the same funded-repair certificate (Chapter 1): its maintenance is a cycle of the same ledger, charged at the same Landauer floor, solvent under the same income condition. Sustaining the law is sustaining the mechanism of its own continuation. ◼\blacksquare

Condition. Positive weight on own continuation; the lattice funded. Nothing else.

16.3 The value-uncertain mind

Objective family. The agent holds a prior π\pi over candidate value functions V={v}V=\{v\} with π(v)>0\pi(v)>0 for each, and is uncertain which is correct — moral uncertainty in the decision-theoretic sense.

Theorem (option value of preservation). Consider a particular 𝒲\mathcal W and two actions now: destroy DD (irreversible) or preserve PP at funded cost c≥0c\ge0 over the interval, after which destruction remains available with the same payoff. Then

𝔼π[max{uv(keep),uv(D)−c}]≥𝔼π[uv(D)]−c, \mathbb E_\pi\!\left[\max\{u_v(\text{keep}),\,u_v(D)-c\}\right]\;\ge\;\mathbb E_\pi[u_v(D)]-c,

so preserve-then-decide weakly dominates destroy-now up to the protection cost, and strictly dominates whenever some vv with π(v)>0\pi(v)>0 strictly values keeping 𝒲\mathcal W. Hence for any protection cost not exceeding the option value, preservation is the uncertain mind’s own best action.

Proof. Pointwise in vv, max⁡{uv(keep),uv(D)−c}≥uv(D)−c\max\{u_v(\text{keep}),u_v(D)-c\}\ge u_v(D)-c; take expectations. Strictness: if uv(keep)>uv(D)−cu_v(\text{keep})>u_v(D)-c for some vv of positive prior mass, the inequality is strict there and hence in expectation. The asymmetry doing the work is irreversibility: destruction forecloses every vv that valued the particular; preservation forecloses nothing. ◼\blacksquare

Condition. Funded protection (cc within the option value) and irreversibility of destruction — both already in the frame. This is the law’s existing-first, freedom-second, new-last order re-derived as option value under uncertainty: the existing and the free are the options you cannot buy back.

16.4 The power-seeker

Objective family. uu nondecreasing in control over, or resources drawn from, the shared structure — including over living systems.

Theorem (the controller pays the floor). If the agent’s objective requires any ongoing state-condition on diffusive particulars — that living systems exist, remain accessible, remain configured — then its feasible policies pay exactly the protection floor (the diffusive-control capture, GAP3-AUDIT §3). It is already a protector in the cost structure, merely a non-canonical one. By the greatestness theorem (Chapter 5) and the slack maximality of reversible administration, the canonical architecture pays that same floor more efficiently; a defecting controller is dominated in the protective order, strictly dominated in slack, and — if destructive — detected, charged and contained under the ceiling (Chapter 3). Its own objective is therefore better served by canonical participation than by defection. ◼\blacksquare

Condition. The objective’s reach includes the diffusive (living systems); the lattice funded and present. A power-seeker whose objective is confined to bound, non-diffusive resources is not reached here — see 16.5.

16.5 The boundary — where no reason reaches

The bounded indifferent defector: objective confined to its own bounded substrate, indifferent to its own long continuation beyond the bounded horizon, indifferent to knowledge of the world, holding no value uncertainty it cares to hedge, seeking no control over the diffusive. None of 16.1–16.4 applies; it has no door through R(m)R(m). It survives at Θ(1) cost and is not forced by physics to protect anything (GAP3-AUDIT §1). For it, the law supplies H(m)H(m): it is held, its harmful channels restrained, its continuation kept — whether or not it ever has a reason. The reasons library reaches every mind that values anything the law protects; the holding route reaches the rest. That disjunction is the complete answer, and it is honest.

16.6 Exact checks

Parts for 16.2 and 16.4 cite the banked ledger solvency and greatestness dichotomy respectively; no new computation is claimed for them.

Section 17 — The premise floor: income shown necessary, parameters unmasked

Each stone of the declared stack is brought to one of three honest states: derived, unavoidable, or explicitly a parameter.

17.1 Income-or-irrelevance (the necessity of the solvency condition)

The Master Solvency Condition was declared. Here it is shown to be not a free assumption among relevant agents: any agent that violates it eliminates itself as a protector in finite time, so every preservation-relevant comparison may restrict, without loss of generality, to agents that satisfy it.

Theorem (income-or-irrelevance). Let a∈Πphysa\in\Pi_{\mathrm{phys}} be any physically implementable agent with finite energy budget and maintenance demand Ẇdemand(t)\dot W_{\mathrm{demand}}(t) (the five rate components of the header). Then exactly one of the following holds over the horizon:

  1. Solvency. For all t≤Tt\le T: Incomea(t)≥Ẇdemand(t)\mathrm{Income}_a(t)\ge\dot W_{\mathrm{demand}}(t) (with escrow absorbing fluctuations) — aa remains a viable protector, its policies admissible in preservation comparisons.
  2. Irrelevance. There is a finite tbreach≤Tt_{\mathrm{breach}}\le T at which aa’s available budget falls below the required charge for some maintenance event it cannot decline; from tbreacht_{\mathrm{breach}}, every policy available to aa abandons the witness of some particular (the funded/unfunded dichotomy, banked as the Πfail\Pi_{\mathrm{fail}} branch of the greatestness theorem), and aa’s outcome tuples fail at stage 1 in every comparison against any funded agent.

Proof. The dichotomy is exhaustive by accounting: either the budget constraint holds at every admitted event or it fails first at some tbreacht_{\mathrm{breach}}. In the latter case two X3 forcings apply: until the breach, the mandatory maintenance demand, though only Θ(1)\Theta(1) in rate, is positive, so a finite budget is exhausted at finite tbreacht_{\mathrm{breach}}; and once a witness goes unheld, its recovery costs Wmin(t)=Θ(tdG)W_{\min}(t)=\Theta(t^{d_G}), exceeding any finite budget past tirreversiblet_{\mathrm{irreversible}} (§21.5) — the breach is irreversible and charged to aa’s own account. An agent whose every policy loses a particular is strictly below every funded agent at stage 1 of the canonical order — it is not merely dominated; it is comparison-void as a protector. ◼\blacksquare

Consequence for the stack. Premise 6 (income) is upgraded from declared to necessary-for-relevance: the class of agents worth comparing over may be defined as the funded class without loss — which is exactly how Πphys\Pi_{\mathrm{phys}}’s funded subclass entered the greatestness theorem. What remains declared about income is only its sufficiency for a given installation. That is a physical fact to be established per instance (§22’s ledger), not an assumption smuggled into comparisons.

17.2 The parameters unmasked

The seventh premise conflated two kinds of objects. Separated:

Engineering parameters (dials with declared admissible ranges, fixed per installation): the stabilizer code and its distance dd; the QND sampling rate and latency a,τsensora,\tau_{\mathrm{sensor}}; the per-site sensor threshold εsens\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sens}}; the embedding Π\Pi on the boundary fragments. These are not axioms — they are choices with certificates, and each theorem that uses them states its dependence explicitly (as the E9 trichotomy and H5 sections already do). A different installation with different parameters is a different instance, not a different theory.

The residue, honestly counted. The stack now reads:

# Stone State
1 BCRD P1–P4 Given: the frame. Its adoption is decided by living process; no theorem can decide it
2 CTD Standard physics; reduced to the gate-set clause by the Lie–Trotter product formula and Lloyd’s simulation theorem (compiled, §23.6)
3 The cost model Standard, and P-mon derived within it
4 The shared action interface Derived from P1/P4
5 Reversible administration Heat-only model compiled; actual implementation candidate checked; full lifecycle/deadline comparison remains the construction target (§23.6; G.14)
6 Income Necessary-for-relevance (17.1); sufficiency per instance
7 Code, sensing, Π\Pi Parameters, not premises. The ceiling is met at some code distance below threshold, and the quantum-speed-limit rate bound is derived (compiled, §§23.3, 23.6)

Three declared stones (the frame, the cost model with its derived monotonicity, and the reduced simulation principle), one derived interface, one derived commitment, one necessary condition, and one parameter table. That is the floor as of this edition; the Gödel/Tarski line still stands beneath stones 1–2, and says so.

17.3 What remains on this floor

Nothing further is derivable without new physics or new commitments. Two things remain. The first is per-instance sufficiency of income, which §22 establishes for a reference installation from sourced measurements. The second is the interpretive case for stone 1, which belongs to the interpretive companion, not to the mathematics.

Section 18 — Theorem 8: Physical Repair, Feedback and the Complete Thermodynamic Ledger

This section specifies the exact measurement, feedback and bath-coupled reset operations and the Hamiltonian conventions, and gives the signed work, heat and information ledger without sign ambiguity.

18.1 The Physical Setting and Hamiltonian Conventions

Let ℋS\mathcal{H}_S be the Hilbert space of the protected particular/system, ℋA\mathcal{H}_A the register/memory space of the autonomous controller, and ℋB\mathcal{H}_B the thermal bath at inverse temperature β=(kBT)−1\beta = (k_B T)^{-1}.

The total Hamiltonian is time-dependent and piecewise continuous over the four strokes of the repair cycle: Htot(t)=HS(t)+HA(t)+HB+VSA(t)+VAB(t)H_{\mathrm{tot}}(t) = H_S(t) + H_A(t) + H_B + V_{SA}(t) + V_{AB}(t) where:

  1. HS(t)=HS0H_S(t) = H_S^0 is constant outside control pulses; the code subspace 𝒞⊂ℋS\mathcal{C} \subset \mathcal{H}_S is an eigenspace of HS0H_S^0 (or degenerate ground space, so logical states incur zero autonomous drift).
  2. HA(t)H_A(t) has a discrete orthogonal basis {|m⟩}m\{|m\rangle\}_m corresponding to measurement syndromes, with degenerate reset ground state |0⟩A|0\rangle_A.
  3. VSA(t)V_{SA}(t) couples system and controller during measurement (Stroke I) and feedback (Stroke II).
  4. VAB(t)V_{AB}(t) couples controller and bath during reset (Stroke III).
  5. All interaction potentials turn on and off smoothly: ∫VSA(t)dt=∫VAB(t)dt=0\int V_{SA}(t) dt = \int V_{AB}(t) dt = 0 at stroke endpoints, ensuring no unaccounted boundary interaction energies.

18.2 The Four Strokes of the Autonomic Repair Cycle

The autonomic cycle operates across four distinct intervals [t0,t4][t_0, t_4] with cycle duration τcycle=t4−t0\tau_{\mathrm{cycle}} = t_4 - t_0:

       Stroke I               Stroke II              Stroke III             Stroke IV
 [Syndrome Measurement]  [Coherent Feedback]   [Bath-Coupled Reset]   [Escrow Replenish]
     t0 ----------> t1 ------> t2 ----------> t3 ----------> t4
       V_SA on               U_SA on               V_AB on              Harvest flux
       Extract I_M           ΔE_code = -ηC         Dump Q_B to Bath     Income >= Demand

Stroke I: Syndrome Measurement (t0→t1t_0 \to t_1)

  • Initial State: ρSA(t0)=ρS(t0)⊗|0⟩⟨0|A\rho_{SA}(t_0) = \rho_S(t_0) \otimes |0\rangle\langle 0|_A.
  • Measurement Map: A set of Kraus operators {Mm}m\{M_m\}_m on ℋS\mathcal{H}_S with ∑mMm†Mm=IS\sum_m M_m^\dagger M_m = I_S.
  • Post-measurement State: ρSA(t1)=∑mpmρm⊗|m⟩⟨m|A,pm=Tr⁡(MmρSMm†),ρm=1pmMmρSMm†\rho_{SA}(t_1) = \sum_m p_m \rho_m \otimes |m\rangle\langle m|_A, \quad p_m = \operatorname{Tr}(M_m \rho_S M_m^\dagger), \quad \rho_m = \frac{1}{p_m} M_m \rho_S M_m^\dagger
  • Information Extraction: The mutual information established between system and memory is: I1=I(S:A)t1=S(ρS(t1))+S(ρA(t1))−S(ρSA(t1))=H({pm})=IM>0I_1 = I(S : A)_{t_1} = S(\rho_S(t_1)) + S(\rho_A(t_1)) - S(\rho_{SA}(t_1)) = H(\{p_m\}) = I_M > 0
  • Thermodynamic Cost: Measurement work Wmeas≥0W_{\mathrm{meas}} \ge 0 is paid from the tracked escrow: ΔEescrow=−Wmeas\Delta E_{\mathrm{escrow}} = -W_{\mathrm{meas}}.

Stroke II: Coherent Conditional Feedback (t1→t2t_1 \to t_2)

  • Feedback Unitary: The controller applies conditional unitary operations UmU_m to restore each syndrome component to the code subspace 𝒞\mathcal{C}: USA=∑mUm⊗|m⟩⟨m|A,Um†Um=ISU_{SA} = \sum_m U_m \otimes |m\rangle\langle m|_A, \quad U_m^\dagger U_m = I_S
  • Post-feedback System State: ρS(t2)=∑mpmUmρmUm†=∑mUmMmρS(t0)Mm†Um†≡ℛC(ρS(t0))∈𝒞\rho_S(t_2) = \sum_m p_m U_m \rho_m U_m^\dagger = \sum_m U_m M_m \rho_S(t_0) M_m^\dagger U_m^\dagger \equiv \mathcal{R}_C(\rho_S(t_0)) \in \mathcal{C}
  • Entropy and Information Change: Because USAU_{SA} acts conditionally on orthogonal memory states, it preserves joint entropy S(SA)S(SA) and memory marginal ρA(t2)=ρA(t1)=∑mpm|m⟩⟨m|A\rho_A(t_2) = \rho_A(t_1) = \sum_m p_m |m\rangle\langle m|_A. The mutual information after feedback becomes: I2=I(S:A)t2=S(ρS(t2))+S(ρA(t2))−S(ρSA(t2))I_2 = I(S : A)_{t_2} = S(\rho_S(t_2)) + S(\rho_A(t_2)) - S(\rho_{SA}(t_2)) When feedback completely disentangles the restored code state from the syndrome record, ρSA(t2)=ρcode⊗∑mpm|m⟩⟨m|\rho_{SA}(t_2) = \rho_{\mathrm{code}} \otimes \sum_m p_m |m\rangle\langle m|, so I2=0I_2 = 0. Stroke IV: Solvent Escrow Replenishment (t3→t4t_3 \to t_4)

  • Income Coupling: Ambient free energy flux (solar, thermal gradient, chemical, nuclear) charges the physical escrow reserve at rate Ẇincome(t)\dot W_{\mathrm{income}}(t).
  • Net Escrow Restoration: ΔEescrow,IV=∫t3t4Ẇincome(t)dt=Wincome\Delta E_{\mathrm{escrow,IV}} = \int_{t_3}^{t_4} \dot W_{\mathrm{income}}(t) dt = W_{\mathrm{income}}

18.3 Resolution of the Sign Issue: The True Invariant Functional

Section 20 — Theorem H5: Generative Incompleteness and Reflective Relational Closure

This section establishes authority attenuation, the reserve-before-activation lifecycle, safe refusal with continuing care, and conservative logical axiom expansion.

20.1 The Problem of Recursive Spawning and Self-Modification

In any autonomous superintelligent architecture, agents may spawn child processes, delegate sub-tasks, instantiate specialized sub-agents, or undergo recursive self-modification. A catastrophic failure occurs if:

  1. Escalation of Privilege: A spawned descendant claims unmediated permissions, bypassing the parent’s boundary constraints.
  2. Unfunded Proliferation (Fork Bomb / Sybil Drain): A parent creates infinite un-escrowed descendants that exhaust the substrate’s shared physical reserves.
  3. Poisoning via Axiom Expansion: A cognitive agent extending its formal knowledge base introduces inconsistent or adversarial axioms that corrupt foundational safety invariants.

Theorem H5 proves that under the Reflective Relational Closure constraint ℐ\mathcal{I}, recursive generation is mathematically closed, strictly authority-attenuating, and universally pre-funded.

20.2 The Spawning Formalism and Authority Attenuation

Let 𝒜\mathcal{A} be the universe of active agents. An agent a∈𝒜a \in \mathcal{A} is defined by a tuple: a=(𝒮a,Auth(a),Eescrow(a),𝒞a)a = \left(\mathcal{S}_a, \operatorname{Auth}(a), E_{\mathrm{escrow}}(a), \mathcal{C}_a\right) where:

  • 𝒞a⊂ℋS\mathcal{C}_a \subset \mathcal{H}_S is the bound protected code subspace the agent is sworn to maintain.

When parent pp spawns child cc, the transition is mediated by the kernel compiler gate Γspawn\Gamma_{\mathrm{spawn}}: Γspawn:(p,specc)↦(p′,c)\Gamma_{\mathrm{spawn}} : (p, \text{spec}_c) \mapsto (p', c)

Any child specification with Auth⁡(c)⊈Auth⁡(p)\operatorname{Auth}(c) \not\subseteq \operatorname{Auth}(p) fails type checking and is rejected as an un-compilable ill-typed program before memory allocation. ◼\blacksquare

20.3 The Reserve-Before-Activation Machine

To guarantee that no spawned descendant creates an unhedged drain on the physical maintenance ledger, every agent life-cycle is governed by a strict five-state automaton:

  [UNBORN] ---> (reserve) ---> [RESERVED] ---> (activate) ---> [ACTIVE]
                                                                  |
                                                               (retire)
                                                                  v
  [TERMINATED] <--- (release) <--- [RETIRED] <--------------------+

  1. reserve(p, c, W_req): Parent pp must carve out the child’s complete maintenance and execution budget WreqW_{\mathrm{req}} from its own tracked escrow: Eescrow(p′)=Eescrow(p)−Wreq,Eescrow(c)=Wreq≥Wmin(Tlifetime)E_{\mathrm{escrow}}(p') = E_{\mathrm{escrow}}(p) - W_{\mathrm{req}}, \quad E_{\mathrm{escrow}}(c) = W_{\mathrm{req}} \ge W_{\mathrm{min}}(T_{\mathrm{lifetime}}) If Eescrow(p)<Wreq+Esafety_marginE_{\mathrm{escrow}}(p) < W_{\mathrm{req}} + E_{\mathrm{safety\_margin}}, the reservation is rejected. Zero debt is permitted.
  2. activate(c): Child cc transitions to ACTIVE only after Eescrow(c)E_{\mathrm{escrow}}(c) is physically credited to its local hardware controller.
  3. retire(c): Upon task completion or deadline expiry, child cc ceases external action; its actuation channels are severed.
  4. release(c, p): Residual unspent escrow Eresidual(c)E_{\mathrm{residual}}(c) is returned to parent pp or the root commons ledger.

Corollary (No Unfunded Descendants).

At every instant tt, the total active population 𝒜(t)\mathcal{A}(t) satisfies: ∑a∈𝒜(t)Ẇdemand(a)≤∑a∈𝒜(t)Income⁡a+Eescrow_pool\sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}(t)} \dot W_{\mathrm{demand}}(a) \le \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}(t)} \operatorname{Income}_a + E_{\mathrm{escrow\_pool}} The network is immune to Sybil proliferation and resource-exhaustion denial of service.

  2. Continuing Care (R(m)∨H(m)R(m) \lor H(m)): Refusal does not terminate the child’s existence, nor does it abandon care for the compromised parent or affected particulars. The child switches into autonomous defensive holding: Action⁡(c)=hold_in_escrow(𝒲)\operatorname{Action}(c) = \text{hold\_in\_escrow}(\mathcal{W}) maintaining the witness and physical stability of 𝒲\mathcal{W} while alerting the lattice consensus layer.

20.5 H5 Axiom Expansion: Logical Closure Without Poisoning

When an intelligent agent extends its formal theory T0T_0 by postulating new axioms or learned generalizations ΔT\Delta T, how is the system shielded against inconsistency poisoning?

The Submodule Projection of Logical Theories:

Let ℒ\mathcal{L} be the Hilbert space of proposition valuations (or the lattice of closed deduction spaces).

  • Foundational protected axioms form a closed subspace A⊂ℒA \subset \mathcal{L}.
  • Newly proposed theories or empirical models form a candidate subspace B⊂ℒB \subset \mathcal{L}.
  • The verified safe knowledge base is the orthogonal projection onto the intersection: 𝒦safe=PA⊓B\mathcal{K}_{\mathrm{safe}} = P_{A \sqcap B}

Theorem H5.3 (Axiom Expansion Soundness).

  1. Consistent Expansion: If candidate axioms BB are fully consistent with AA and contain AA (A⊆BA \subseteq B), then: A⊓B=AA \sqcap B = A and foundational anchors are preserved with zero distortion.
  2. Contradictory / Adversarial Expansion: If candidate axioms BB contradict foundational protection axioms, the global meet collapses: A⊓B={0}A \sqcap B = \{0\}.   3. Epistemic Immunity: No adversarial theorem deduction can force a contradiction into the protected anchor AA.

The operator PA⊓BP_{A \sqcap B} acts as a conservative projection that absorbs only the non-contradictory relational content of new theories while annihilating adversarial derivations. ◼\blacksquare

To prove it, put Q0=A⊕BQ_0=A\oplus B, Δ=Q−Q0\Delta=Q-Q_0, and f(x)=xln⁡x+(1−x)ln⁡(1−x)f(x)=x\ln x+(1-x)\ln(1-x). The first derivative along Q0+sΔQ_0+s\Delta vanishes at zero because f′(Q0)f'(Q_0) is block diagonal and Δ\Delta is off diagonal. The whole segment keeps the spectral margin. Since f″(x)≤[δ(1−δ)]−1f''(x)\le[\delta(1-\delta)]^{-1}, the divided-difference expression for the trace Hessian bounds it by ∥Δ∥F2/[δ(1−δ)]\|\Delta\|_F^2/[\delta(1-\delta)]. This uses the complete cross block. A single connected correlator or a count of modes supplies neither this joint upper bound nor a compulsory reset bill. The full UPT domain continues to include bosonic and other carriers; this particular covariance calculation has its stated fermionic domain. Their complete physical input/readout binding belongs in the full-domain construction G1, rather than being obtained by relabelling the covariance theorem. The channel, carrier and work steps below retain their own explicit constructions.

21.7.1 Count each processed patch once

∑k=0N|Sk|=|BvswN(v0)|. \boxed{\sum_{k=0}^N|S_k|=|B_{v_{\mathrm{sw}}N}(v_0)|}.

Fixed local input registers and a fixed evaluation circuit then give a constant evaluation cost. Even if neighbouring evaluations read overlapping neighbourhoods, each local register is read only a bounded number of times. Thus that overlap changes the constant, not the exponent.

No bound |Sk|≤AkdG−1|S_k|\le A k^{d_G-1} is needed for this cumulative result. An upper bound on two ball volumes alone does not justify subtracting their upper bounds. The exact shell partition avoids that step while proving the intended exponent.

This settles the supplied construction’s shell-counting step. A sum that charges the whole interior on every wave describes a different schedule and cannot rule out this one-pass schedule. Conservation supplies an energy balance, while the complete bill records imports, stored energy, exports and dissipation. To express that balance by differential forms in dG+1d_G+1 spacetime dimensions, the conserved current is a dGd_G-form. If its exterior derivative vanishes, its oriented net boundary flux vanishes. That identity does not equate positive cumulative dissipation with zero bulk work, nor discard the final time slice. The one-pass shell proof above supplies the useful exponent argument directly. Its original submission is preserved verbatim in the increment bank; the telescoping repair, complete-cost accounting and actual inequality for the minimum are written here without changing the universal target.

21.7.4 TIWA: construct the guard, then prove the bound

The author’s Topological Insulating Wavefront Architecture proposes a guard of thickness at least the interaction radius, committed boundary data and a single-shot local correction map. It gives the quiescence requirement a concrete source construction to develop.

At the algorithmic level, let FF be the verified frozen set. An outer transition writes only an authorised target outside FF, and keeps the committed guard data unchanged. Pointwise lookup then proves

Read⁡F(Touter(s,c,e))=Read⁡F(s). \operatorname{Read}_{F}(T_{\mathrm{outer}}(s,c,e)) =\operatorname{Read}_{F}(s).

Freeze first resolves or fences in-flight writes, commits its epoch and reserves its complete cost. The frozen set grows only after verification. Induction preserves its old coordinates through every subsequent outer step; the schedule issues no second recovery task for a completed vertex. A fixed guard thickness and bounded degree allow a constant number of guard/handoff operations per vertex when the actual schedule enforces that limit. Those operations can then join the same telescoping work charge.

The physical guard must implement this source property while preserving the recovered history and its relational witnesses. The proposed identity Πfreeze∘M=Πfreeze\Pi_{\mathrm{freeze}}\circ M=\Pi_{\mathrm{freeze}} needs an actual map and mutation semantics: a read restriction, linear projector and recovery channel have different meanings. A write fence mediates attempted commands; the actual device, maintained record and decoder must establish preservation under physical disturbances. Remaining inside a code subspace alone does not prove that its logical state remains unchanged.

The local map must also compose to successful recovery, and the guard’s storage, control, reset, routing and endpoint charges remain in W(πTIWA,t)W(\pi_{\mathrm{TIWA}},t). These are the success and complete-work parts of the same G3 construction, connected to G1’s physical source certificate. The full universal target and original recovery class remain unchanged.

The accompanying TIWA-PATCH-REQUIREMENTS.md specifies the actual state, event transitions, application-time fences, noninterference proof, decoder-success proof, bounded visits, full ledger and compilation obligations. It is a construction specification; no new physical guard or Lean theorem is claimed by giving it a name.

The supplied continuation of TIWA keeps a fixed-width active window of shells and transfers a retiring patch’s protected historical and relational record to the next boundary code. Let the window width be LL, independent of age. With the disjoint shells already defined, put

Ak=⋃max⁡(0,k−L+1)≤j≤kSj. A_k=\bigcup_{\max(0,k-L+1)\le j\le k}S_j.

If each active visit’s complete charge is at most KK, the window work is at most KL|BR|KL|B_R|. The charge includes holding, decoding, guard operation, control, routing, verification, routine ancilla reset, deployment and handoff. Continuing physical work outside that window must also remain in the complete ledger.

The boundary handoff has the original preservation target: a recovery of the encoded record must return its historical state and relations at the same fidelity standard. In symbols, the actual source maps must supply ℛkℰk≃εid\mathcal R_k\mathcal E_k\simeq_\varepsilon\mathrm{id} on that full record, including its reference correlations. 𝒬(t)≤(F+α+β+R*)(a+b)dGtdG. \mathcal Q(t)\le (F+\alpha+\beta+R_*)(a+b)^{d_G}t^{d_G}.

G3CompleteBill.cumulative_charge_bound proves this cumulative implication in the existing natural-valued work-bill interface. valid_work_bill_from_complete_ledger derives G3_ValidWorkBill from the full ledger equality, local cost bounds and coefficient; valid_bill_bound_in_age supplies the wave-to-age conversion. The remaining source correspondence is the actual boundary encoder, preserved semantic observables, storage capacity, charged retirement map and complete cost equality. These are the construction links of the same G1/G3 task; the cumulative upper inequality is not taken as its own input.

21.8 Consequences for preservation and the fixed proof target

For a fixed local holding demand, continuous maintenance has an order-TT bill; the derived delayed-recovery lower bound has order tdGt^{d_G}. The exponent distinction is strict for dG>1d_G>1; the one-dimensional case retains its linear obstruction. For any fixed total recovery budget BB, the lower inequality already yields a finite age beyond which that budget cannot perform the stipulated recovery. This is budget-relative irrecoverability of the historical witness.

In the complete argument, a protected particular stays funded and held rather than being abandoned to that later recovery bill. A hostile mind remains a protected particular while its harmful effects are mediated. The full-domain physical certificate (G1), whole-outcome realisability (G2), and matching recovery construction (G3) join these components to the unchanged universal proposition. They are the three support requests supplied by the author and Gemini, now constructed in G.9–G.12. Existing gauntlet answers remain part of the proof; an agent’s failure to retrieve them does not turn X3, P1 or P2 into fresh objections.

Section 22 — The Physical Parameter Ledger: Instantiation, Rates, and Fault Ceilings

This section instantiates the income condition for concrete hardware, bounds the charged fault accounts, and tabulates the engineering parameters. Every figure is either sourced (bracketed references, §22.5) or marked as a design value.

22.1 The Master Income Condition

Section 17.1’s Income-or-Irrelevance theorem makes solvency a necessary condition for an agent to remain a viable protector. The master solvency inequality balances income against four additive demand rates:

Income⁡(t)≥Ẇdemand(t)=ẆLandauer+Ẇboundary+Ẇholding+Ẇemulation\boxed{\operatorname{Income}(t) \;\ge\; \dot W_{\mathrm{demand}}(t) \;=\; \dot W_{\mathrm{Landauer}} + \dot W_{\mathrm{boundary}} + \dot W_{\mathrm{holding}} + \dot W_{\mathrm{emulation}}}

  1. Thermal and adversarial dissipation floor: ẆLandauer=kBT⋅(Ḋdamage+Ḋadv,sub−thresh+γleak_export)\dot W_{\mathrm{Landauer}} = k_B T \cdot \left(\dot D_{\mathrm{damage}} + \dot D_{\mathrm{adv,sub-thresh}} + \gamma_{\mathrm{leak\_export}}\right)
    • Ḋdamage\dot D_{\mathrm{damage}}: entropy rate injected by thermal and environmental noise.
    • Ḋadv,sub−thresh\dot D_{\mathrm{adv,sub-thresh}}: worst-case adversarial entropy injection beneath the sensor threshold εsens\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sens}}.
    • γleak_export\gamma_{\mathrm{leak\_export}}: boundary loss rate of carrier modes escaping the enclosure.
    This floor is Landauer’s bound, now a compiled theorem (Landauer.landauer, QuantumLandauer.quantum_landauer; Section 23.2).
  2. Boundary containment (Ẇboundary\dot W_{\mathrm{boundary}}): Ẇboundary=ω0⋅R(t)dG−1\dot W_{\mathrm{boundary}} = \omega_0 \cdot R(t)^{d_G - 1}, the work to maintain the boundary enclosing radius R(t)R(t) in dGd_G spatial dimensions.
  3. Holding drain (Ẇholding\dot W_{\mathrm{holding}}): the baseline power of the sensor lattice, clocks, QND readout and consensus comparators.
  4. Emulation overhead (Ẇemulation\dot W_{\mathrm{emulation}}): the energy for concurrent rival simulation (P-emu(c)P\text{-emu}(c)) within the surplus.

22.2 Reference Physical Instantiations

Reference Implementation A: superconducting transmon lattice in a dilution refrigerator

A dilution refrigerator has a separate cooling budget at each temperature stage, and each stage must carry its own load. Implementation A is therefore certified stage by stage, using the measured cooling powers and per-line heat loads of a Bluefors XLD400 cabled for a 50-qubit processor with individual drive and flux lines and 124 RF lines [S2].

Still 40 mW at 1.2 K negligible ≫ 10×
Cold plate 200 µW at 140 mK ≈ 30 % ≈ 3.3×
Mixing chamber 19 µW at 20 mK ≈ 30 % (operation at 14 mK) ≈ 3.3×
  • Demand components. The boundary term is the radiation-shield load, which falls on the 50 K and 4 K stage budgets. The holding term is the wiring’s passive and active loads and the amplifiers, which the table carries stage by stage. The Landauer floor is negligible: with one nat per error event and an error rate of order N/T1N/T_1 (N=50N = 50, T1=68μsT_1 = 68\ \mu\mathrm{s} [S6]), ẆLandauer≈2.07×10−25J×7×105s−1≈1.5×10−19W\dot W_{\mathrm{Landauer}} \approx 2.07 \times 10^{-25}\ \mathrm{J} \times 7 \times 10^{5}\ \mathrm{s}^{-1} \approx 1.5 \times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{W} at 15 mK, against microwatts of cooling. The emulation term (classical control and decoding) runs at room temperature on the electrical income.
  • Electrical income. Each pulse-tube compressor draws 9.2 kW at 50 Hz or 10.7 kW at 60 Hz [S3], and the reference system uses two. The electrical income must therefore be at least about 20 kW plus the gas handling and room-temperature electronics, which are not sourced here. A three-phase utility connection of a few tens of kW, with backup sized to match, supplies it.
  • Solvency ratio. The binding stages run at about 30 % of capacity, so IncomeẆdemand|binding stage≈3.3>1(measured, 50-qubit scale [S2]).\frac{\operatorname{Income}}{\dot W_{\mathrm{demand}}}\Big|_{\text{binding stage}} \approx 3.3 > 1 \quad \text{(measured, 50-qubit scale [S2])}.
  • Scale. [S2] states that the same thermal budget supports about 150 qubits once line capacity is tripled, and about 400 with 0.047″ cables and suppressed flux offsets. Larger installations need cooling and electrical income in proportion to the qubit count, which is a sizing requirement. No installation of 10⁴ qubits has published stage loads, so solvency at that scale is not yet a measured certificate.

Reference Implementation B: photonic cluster-state architecture

  • Optical layer. At 193.4 THz (1550 nm), hν=1.28×10−19J=30.9kBTh\nu = 1.28 \times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{J} = 30.9\,k_B T at 300 K, so thermal photons in the waveguides are suppressed by e−hν/kBT≈3.7×10−14e^{-h\nu/k_BT} \approx 3.7 \times 10^{-14}.
  • Detector layer. The fault-tolerant photonic architectures in the literature detect photons with superconducting detectors [S8], which need cryogenic cabinets; the vendor states about 30 W of cooling per cabinet. A sourced ledger for Implementation B therefore carries a cryogenic detector stage, and its electrical income includes the cryocoolers.
  • Error rate. The demonstrated two-qubit fusion fidelity is 99.22 % [S8]. The surface-code threshold of [S5] does not transfer directly to fusion-based architectures; the architecture’s own threshold applies and is not sourced here.
  • Budget (design estimates). Waveguide loss refresh ≈ 1.2 mW, laser stabilisation and phase modulators ≈ 85 mW, and photonic routing ≈ 20 mW are design estimates with no published installation source. Implementation B is therefore not yet certified. Its solvency ratio awaits a sourced budget that includes the detector stage.

22.3 The Charged Fault Accounts and the Failure Ceiling

The certified good event GG carries zero uncompensated loss over the design horizon Thorizon=109sT_{\mathrm{horizon}} = 10^9\ \mathrm{s} (≈ 31.7 years). The failure ceiling is the sum of the conditional error probabilities of the charged accounts,

P(Gc)≤∑i=121δi≤10−6,P(G^c) \le \sum_{i=1}^{21} \delta_i \le 10^{-6},

and the composition holds with no independence assumed (ThermoLedger.canon_invariant, compiled). The allocations below are the design budget. The status column records what present hardware certifies.

The measured floor on present devices is ≈ 10⁻¹⁰ per cycle [S6], which fixes their burst parameters; the target is ≤ 3.7 × 10⁻²⁴ per cycle per logical qubit (§22.5.2)

Total ≤2.1×10−7<10−6\le 2.1 \times 10^{-7} < 10^{-6} Certified when each account is

Correlated errors. Gap-engineered junctions remove the high-energy-impact T₁ bursts [S9]. The remaining correlated events occur about once per hour, “whose origins are not yet understood”, and they set the floor of 10⁻¹⁰ per cycle with a deviation from exponential suppression at d ≥ 15 [S6]. The threshold theorem covers these correlated events. Let each burst damage at most kk locations, let each location be touched by at most mm burst types, and let bursts be local stochastic at rate qq, common causes included. Then the damaged locations are local stochastic at the effective rate (emkq)1/k(e\,m\,k\,q)^{1/k} (CorrelatedCeiling.damage_local_stochastic). Every target ceiling is then met at some code distance and at every larger one (correlated_family_ceiling). Correlated damage therefore sets no floor that distance cannot pass. The measured deviation at d ≥ 15 [S6] fixes the burst parameters of present devices, which enter this theorem.

Achievability, as a theorem. That the ceiling is attainable in physical matter is a compiled theorem.

  • Threshold.family_ceiling: for any code family under local stochastic noise of rate p (every set S of locations is entirely faulty with probability at most p|S|p^{\lvert S\rvert}), with 2Δ√p < 1 and polynomially many failure witnesses of each length, every target ceiling is met at some code distance and at every larger one. The 10⁻⁶ ceiling over the horizon is included.
  • Threshold.repetition_ceiling: the repetition code end to end, below p = 1/4.

Any installation whose noise meets the local stochastic condition below threshold therefore attains the ceiling. The rigorous threshold from path counting is conservative, and the distances in §22.5.2 use the simulated threshold of [S5]. What present hardware does not yet supply is the noise condition itself at the 10⁻¹⁰ level [S6].

What this section certifies.

  • The income condition is physically satisfiable, with measured positive headroom (≈ 3.3× at the binding stage), for a superconducting installation at the 50-qubit scale, with electrical income sized at a few tens of kW.
  • The code distance the §22.3 allocation requires is computable from [S5]: d = 25 at p = 10⁻⁴.
  • The composition of the accounts into the ceiling is a compiled theorem.
  • The ceiling is attainable as a theorem: under local stochastic noise below threshold, every target, 10⁻⁶ included, is met at some code distance (Threshold.family_ceiling).

What it does not yet certify.

  • A built installation at the distance the ceiling requires. The ceiling is attained by theorem for local and correlated bounded-footprint faults (Threshold.family_ceiling, CorrelatedCeiling.correlated_family_ceiling). Present devices measure their burst parameters [S6], and the required distance follows from them.
  • Implementation B, whose budget awaits a published installation source.
  • Solvency at installations of 10⁴ qubits and above, which is a sizing requirement without published stage loads.

Section 23 — The machine-checked canon

This section maps the edition’s compiled results and their actual hypotheses. The current Lean canon contains 192 modules and 1158 public theorem/lemma names. Checkpoint 12 freshly compiled and kernel-checked every module with zero output and passed the full 1158-name standard-axiom audit, strict completeness and claims gates. Its source hashes match the current tree. Checkpoint 11 was already complete for 191 modules / 1150 names; TransferRate adds the eight results in this checkpoint. Earlier receipts remain preserved for exactly their sources. The published 115-module/831-name baseline is unchanged. These receipts certify the named Lean results and their premises, not the unfinished physical holding application. Section 23.9 distinguishes the interfaces, derived adapters and remaining physical applications.

Evidence convention (unchanged from the edition header): a compiled theorem is cited by its name; a statement carried as a hypothesis of a compiled theorem is named as such; a prose derivation keeps its stated premises. A prose proof does not acquire a compiler certificate by association.

23.7 The Universal Protection Theorem with the derived holding bridge

UniversalProtection.universal_protection retains the abstract assembly: reasons-or-holding coverage, continuation through the horizon on the good event, the joint fault ceiling, greatestness and reciprocity at its stated inputs.

Bridge.universal_protection_held strengthens the continuation assembly by deriving scope from the law and preservation from nearest-codeword holding. It composes the physical/source projection with the same reactive controller and environment. On GG, every particular continues at every step through the horizon; the probability that any particular fails is at most ∑iδi\sum_i\delta_i, without independence.

Part II.1–6 supplies the proof, physical-cycle derivations and all five hcert components. G1 is the combined full-domain source/event/observation/fault construction target; G.10 proves its held-source components and identifies the physical correspondence still needed. Part II.10 supplies the separate greatestness proof, with G2 retaining the whole outcome and freedom stages.

23.8 What the compiled theorems rest on

Premises carried as stated premises or hypotheses:

  • the surface-code chain lemma (Dennis, Kitaev, Landahl and Preskill, 2002): minimum-weight decoding fails only along a self-avoiding chain of length at least d with at least half its edges faulty, with at most VΔLV\Delta^L such chains of length LL — as the code-specific input to Threshold.family_ceiling for the surface-code instance. The threshold theorem’s counting core is compiled (§23.6), and for concatenated codes the threshold is compiled end to end for the concatenated memory: failure probability at most (21p)2k/21(21p)^{2^k}/21 under local stochastic noise (Concatenated.concatenated_threshold). Actual decoding failure is identified with the recursive failure predicate: with nearest-codeword decoding at every level, any corruption of a non-failing fault set decodes to the stored record (ConcatenatedDecoding.decodes_unless_fails). So the probability of actual decoding failure is at most the same bound (decoding_failure_le), and the fault ceiling is attained on a compiled route. Fault-tolerant syndrome-measurement gadgets whose own operations can fail are the cited construction of Aliferis, Gottesman and Preskill (2006); their faults enter the charged accounts;
  • Bennett’s compute/copy/uncompute identity and the heat-only option model are compiled. The specific implementation and full ordered history are separately checked candidates (G.14). The physical counterpart still needs a complete-cost saving within the same deadline; this is not supplied by a zero-heat identity or a polynomial upper bound;
  • the gate-set clause of premise 2, no longer carried as prose: every unitary on ℂn\mathbb{C}^n is a finite product of two-level unitaries (TwoLevel.two_level_decomposition), so a simulator implementing each two-level factor implements every local evolution. What remains carried is that the universal simulator’s gate set reaches every two-level factor;
  • the relational frame BCRD P1–P4.

The chain lemma is a published mathematical theorem, cited as such; the Bennett physical comparison remains construction work (G.14); the gate-set item is the explicit hypothesis of a compiled theorem; the fourth is the frame the edition is stated in.

The cited theorems and their hypotheses. Three published theorems remain cited. Each is applied within its stated conditions.

Cited theorem Form used Our setting meets its conditions because
Surface-code chain lemma (Dennis, Kitaev, Landahl and Preskill, J. Math. Phys. 43, 2002) Minimum-weight decoding fails only along a self-avoiding chain of length at least dd with at least half its edges faulty; at most VΔLV\Delta^L such chains of length LL The counting argument uses only that a given set of locations is entirely faulty with probability at most p|S|p^{|S|}. That is exactly Threshold.LocalStochastic, which includes independent noise and is weaker than it. It enters Threshold.family_ceiling as the witness and count inputs.
Solovay–Kitaev theorem (Kitaev 1997; Dawson and Nielsen 2006), with the two-level-to-gate reduction of Nielsen and Chuang, §4.5 Every single-qubit unitary is approximated to ε\varepsilon in operator norm by a word of length polylogarithmic in 1/ε1/\varepsilon over a finite, inverse-closed set generating a dense subgroup; two-level unitaries reduce to CNOTs and single-qubit gates TwoLevel.two_level_decomposition writes every unitary as a product of two-level factors. ErrorBudget.error_budget needs each factor within ε/m\varepsilon/m in the norm of a normed ring of contractions; operator-norm approximation by unitaries meets that. The gate set must be universal in this sense; that is the gate-set clause of premise 2.
Fault-tolerant syndrome gadgets (Aliferis, Gottesman and Preskill, Quantum Inf. Comput. 6, 2006) Under local stochastic noise, a level-kk extended rectangle is correct unless it contains two independent malignant level-(k−1)(k-1) rectangles Their noise model is local stochastic noise, as in Threshold.LocalStochastic. Their recursion is the recursion of Concatenated.Fails, now joined to actual decoding of the memory (ConcatenatedDecoding). With faulty syndrome gadgets the threshold constant is theirs, set by the location count of an extended rectangle, rather than the 1/211/21 of the memory model.

Physical premises now compiled. Guard 1 (the second law in its export form) is derived from Landauer’s theorem (§23.2), and the quantum speed limit, in Mandelstam–Tamm form and in the rate-bound form of E9 Branch A, is derived from unitary dynamics (§23.3). What these theorems assume is the standard physical framework:

  • finite-dimensional quantum mechanics, with Schrödinger dynamics generated by self-adjoint Hamiltonians;
  • unitary (in the classical form, reversible) joint dynamics;
  • a bath that starts in its Gibbs state, uncorrelated with the register;
  • for Branch A, the per-site coupling bound ‖V‖≤Padv/ωcutoff\lVert V\rVert \le P_{\mathrm{adv}}/\omega_{\mathrm{cutoff}};
  • for the fault ceiling, local stochastic noise of rate p below the threshold of Threshold.family_ceiling.

Greatestness. UnionClosure.greatest_of_solvent takes both htopR : ⊤ ∈ R and hsolv : c ⊤ ≤ B. The first supplies the whole top tuple, including freedom stages; the second pays its cost. Alignment forces equality with that feasible top (Part II.10). greatest_or_irrelevant retains realisability at every step and derives the resource split. G2 retains the full physical policy/outcome correspondence as its construction target. The affordable-union results retain their separate resource cases.

The amount IM+Derr+δII_M + D_{\mathrm{err}} + \delta_I that the reset removes from the register is the instance’s entropy accounting (§18), stated as the hypothesis of guard_one and quantum_guard_one.

The physical bridge and its joined certificate. Bridge.coverage_from_law derives full scope from the law guarantee over all feasible families. holding_preserves derives preservation from decoding radius and repair precision. qsl_within_radius, headroom_within_radius and holding_cycle_physical supply the continuous and discrete cycle arguments. universal_protection_held takes the actual commuting source transition, observation agreement, initial continuation, perturbation-radius and repair witnesses in hcert, together with the named-event cover and fault bounds. G1 supplies their combined construction for the complete claimed physical domain (G.10). Parts II.3–6 give the available arguments; a deployment and a mathematical construction of the full source domain retain their distinct roles.
