The quantum-coherence branch: the warm start and the open problem (WarmStart). Balasubramanian, Davydova and Lin prove a passive memory in ℝ3\mathbb R^3 for the thermal encoding (arXiv:2605.10943, Theorems 1.1 and 2.6, via Chesi, Loss, Bravyi and Terhal, New J. Phys. 12, 025013, 2010). The open step is preparing an initial state the theorem covers.

Call a prepared syndrome law μ\mu a warm start when μ≤Cπ\mu\le C\pi pointwise, with π\pi the thermal syndrome law. A warm start stays dominated at every time: μKt≤Cπ\mu K^t\le C\pi (warm_start), and every event has probability at most Cπ(A)C\,\pi(A) (warm_start_event). Tracking the protected logical observables then gives a drift of the decoded qubit of at most t⋅poly(n)⋅CTr(P⟂ρβ)t\cdot\mathrm{poly}(n)\cdot\sqrt{C\,\mathrm{Tr}(P^\perp\rho_\beta)}. Chesi et al.’s hypotheses make Pℒ†(X̃)P=0P\mathcal L^\dagger(\tilde X)P=0, so only leakage from PP moves ⟨X̃⟩\langle\tilde X\rangle. A warm start with C=poly(n)C=\mathrm{poly}(n) therefore preserves the exponential lifetime, with its exponent halved. This derivation is recorded with its sources and is not compiled.

The empty syndrome is not a warm start: its constant is 1/π(∅)=eΘ(n)1/\pi(\emptyset)=e^{\Theta(n)}.

An exhaustive computation on the construction itself shows that a fixed-range polymer route cannot supply the warm start. The construction is built algebraically from the paper’s §3.2.2, and the build verifies δ1δ0=0\delta^1\delta^0=0 and one logical qubit at every level computed. The metachecks of level ii are stretched by the scale factor ℓ\ell at each later level. In the computed cases, all dependencies are generated within radius 4 at level 1 and within radius 12 at level 2, with ℓ=3\ell=3. Hence for every fixed range a single violated check passes all local metachecks yet is invalid.

Section G.21 develops a constructive full-history polymer sampler for the ideal thermal syndrome law, with its counting theorem and source correspondence stated explicitly. It avoids the failed product/deletion hypothesis and does not require a preparation mixing estimate. WarmStart.fibre_reassembly and reverse_sampler_bound give the exact probability-composition algebra. pointwise_from_absolute retains the probability floor whenever an absolute-error estimate is used. The actual noisy preparation/handoff and complete-cost application remain unfinished; the maximal quantum-coherence target is retained in full.

G.21 Constructive thermal preparation from the complete decoding history

Working derivation for author review, 26 October 2026. The generic support lemmas are compiled. The ideal sampler’s source application is audited in prose. The endpoint compensation, anisotropic feedback and complete controller-degree derivations are now included below; the installation’s joint endpoint-kernel correspondence remains explicit. The target is the actual BDL thermal syndrome law with a polynomial, preferably constant, one-sided pointwise factor. This does not assume product zero-excess fibres, a local mixing gap, an initially warm raw state or a reset of protected quantum data.

1. Retain the full deterministic history

For one syndrome sector of C(2k), introduce one binary variable for every syndrome coordinate at every level:

h = (s_2k, s_(2k-1), ..., s_0).

Fix all local tie-breaks in the published coarse-graining maps, with the zero input producing zero corrections. A valid finest syndrome determines exactly one history. Conversely, the following finite local constraints characterize such histories:

  • For an R_X step, use (L1), (L2), (L3) of STEP2-FINE-CONDITIONAL.md, with the coarse output stored as the next layer’s variables.
  • For an R_Z step, use the local cohomology-class reduction in Theorem 4.6. The difference from the lifted coarse value is a local coboundary.
  • The constant-sized seed syndrome s_0 must belong to its actual image(delta).

Backward induction using s_i=delta(f_i)+F_i(s_(i-1)) proves global validity at every level. Forward evaluation of the fixed local rules proves uniqueness. These are constraints on syndrome variables; f_i is computed, not summed over as an additional freely degenerate variable.

Each constraint has bounded scope and each coordinate appears in boundedly many constraints, uniformly in k. The bounds depend on the fixed gadget size, Tanner degrees and subdivision parameter. The seed constraint has constant scope. Make the primal graph G by connecting every pair of coordinates in a common constraint scope. Its degree Delta is bounded independently of k. Its number M of vertices is polynomial in the physical block size (indeed at most the sum of the level sizes). Let S bound each scope and I the number of scopes reading one coordinate. The fixed gadget and Tanner incidences give constants S and I independent of the code level. An intermediate coordinate is read only by the two adjacent coarse steps, so I does not grow with hierarchy depth. Explicitly, Delta<=I(S-1). The finite tests’ observed degrees are not substituted for this uniform symbolic bound.

The local source correspondence is BDL Theorems 4.6 and 4.7, Remarks 4.4–4.5, and the bounded-degree construction. Their Section 5.2 already records full decoding histories and proves componentwise coarse-graining. The primal graph used here includes whole constraint scopes, so component restriction does not assume the stronger product property that failed numerically.

2. Derive the history energy bound

Write the history in the finest-to-coarsest direction. Every R_Z step is non-increasing in syndrome weight; every R_X step reduces it by at least one half. The two steps alternate. Thus, in either sector,

|s_(i-2)| <= |s_i|/2,
sum_i |s_i| <= 2 sum_(j>=0) 2^(-j) |s_2k| <= 4 |s_2k|.

This holds for every valid history, including a history obtained by restricting to one connected support component. It is a support/energy inequality on the complete history, not a fixed-range metacheck assumption.

3. Connected components give an exact polymer representation

The all-zero history satisfies every constraint. Let h be valid and let Gamma be a connected component of its occupied coordinates in G. Setting all other coordinates to zero leaves a valid history:

  • a constraint touching Gamma cannot touch another occupied component, because its scope is a clique;
  • on that scope the restricted assignment either agrees with h or is zero;
  • both assignments satisfy the constraint in the respective case.

Conversely, the union of pairwise nonadjacent valid connected supports is valid by the same scope argument. Hence there is an exact bijection between histories and compatible polymer families. A polymer is a nonempty connected support Gamma whose standalone binary assignment satisfies every constraint.

Let E(Gamma) count its occupied finest-level coordinates. The previous bound applied to that standalone valid history gives

E(Gamma) >= |Gamma|/4 > 0.

There is no zero-energy polymer. Its activity at z=exp(-beta) is the monomial w_Gamma(z)=z^E(Gamma). Energy is additive on disjoint components. The polymer partition function is therefore exactly the thermal partition function on valid finest syndromes: there is no uncounted fibre multiplicity.

4. Verify convergence with explicit constants

Put B=(Delta+1)^2. A rooted depth-first traversal bounds the number of connected supports of size ell containing a fixed vertex by B^ell. There is at most one binary polymer assignment on a given support.

An incompatible polymer meets the closed neighbourhood of Gamma, of size at most (Delta+1)|Gamma|. For r=B e |z|^(1/4),

sum_(eta incompatible Gamma) |w_eta(z)| exp(|eta|)
   <= (Delta+1)|Gamma| sum_(ell>=1) r^ell
   = (Delta+1)|Gamma| r/(1-r).

For example choose the complex fugacity disk

delta = [1/(4 e B (Delta+2))]^4.

Then r<1/[4(Delta+2)] throughout |z|<delta, so the displayed sum is less than |Gamma|. This is the Kotecky–Preiss criterion, derived here from the actual history bound. Taking the device temperature sufficiently low that 0<z_0<delta, as well as below BDL’s memory threshold, gives uniform slack.

The algorithmic counting hypotheses are also explicit: connected supports of size ell can be listed in exp(O(ell+log M)); testing their local constraints and computing E takes polynomial time in ell; activities are monomials of order at least |Gamma|/4; and the full partition polynomial has degree at most the number of finest checks, hence at most M. The same convergence bound holds after deleting any set of polymers.

Helmuth–Perkins–Regts Theorem 2.2 and Lemma 2.8 in Section 2.6 then supply a deterministic relative partition-function approximation for every remaining polymer set. This application uses their general bounded-degree polymer result, not an unsupported transfer of their Potts-model conclusion.

5. Truncate with a one-sided pointwise guarantee

Set q=B z_0^(1/4)<1. In a positive repulsive polymer gas, P(Gamma present)<=w_Gamma. A union bound gives

P(some polymer has size > L)
   <= M sum_(ell>L) q^ell
   = M q^(L+1)/(1-q).

Choose L=O(log M) so this is at most 1/2. The exact gas restricted to polymers of size at most L is the full thermal law conditioned on that event, and hence is pointwise at most twice the full law. Missing rare large-polymer configurations causes no problem for this one-sided bound.

List the P<=poly(M) remaining polymers. Visit them once in a fixed order. If a polymer conflicts with one already selected, skip it. Otherwise the exact conditional inclusion probability is

p = w_Gamma Z(remaining compatible with Gamma)
    / [Z(remaining without Gamma)
       + w_Gamma Z(remaining compatible with Gamma)].

Both partition functions are for deleted-polymer submodels. Approximate each within exp(+-eta), eta=1/(16P). The resulting probability and its complement are each at most exp(2eta) times their exact values.

This is finite feed-forward self-reduction, with no Markov-chain mixing. Its pointwise guarantee follows by multiplying the conditional branch factors, rather than converting a TV estimate without a probability floor.

6. Keep the randomness and work pathwise bounded

Exact rational-coin rejection is unnecessary. Inclusion has p<=1/2 since w_Gamma<=1 and the compatible partition function is at most the unrestricted one. Clamp the approximate probability to at most 1/2, then round it down to a dyadic grid of spacing d<=1/(16P). Sample it with a fixed b=O(log P) unbiased random bits.

Rounding down only decreases the inclusion probability. It increases the exclusion probability by at most d; the true exclusion probability is at least 1/2. Thus either branch is at most

exp(2eta)+2d <= exp(1/(4P))

times the true branch probability. Over all P visits the factor is at most exp(1/4)<2. Combining with truncation gives

mu_sector <= 4 pi_sector.

All enumeration, counting calls, branch decisions and random-bit use have a deterministic polynomial bound in M. The history and used random bits can be retained in the existing complete ledger. This is not an expected- work substitution.

For the two independent CSS syndrome sectors the joint factor multiplies: mu_joint<=16 pi_joint. The exponent p in A n^p can be zero. No maximum-of- sector-factors shortcut is used.

7. Preserve the unknown logical state and its reference

Sample the syndrome independently of the unknown logical input. For each sampled s, use the published decoder’s Pauli representative O_s, with delta(O_s)=s, on the encoded logical state. The branch encoder V_s is an isometry, and its matching decoder has D_s V_s=I. The controlled branch record is retained. Linearity extends this identity to every joint logical- reference state. ChannelExtension.ext_recovers_reference supplies the existing isometric-reference algebra; the branch circuit must be identified with it. There is no replacement by a fixed default logical state.

The following reference-norm derivation keeps the arbitrary reference register and the original fault budget. Its ideal warm-start proof and its residual-noise application have distinct statuses.

Verification status

The ideal sampler’s prose source audit checks the local cut-out, uniform scope incidence, exact history/partition bijection and all hypotheses of the published counting theorem, including the polymer-deleted submodels. The generic support, restriction and conditioning bounds are compiled. Finite source tests cover both syndrome sectors and the published seed; they do not replace the all-level source derivation. The external FPTAS is used as a published algorithm, not represented as a separately implemented and kernel-checked solver in this repository. The later subsections construct noise compensation, private Pauli feedback and its controller invoice. Their physical-kernel correspondence and prose scope are stated explicitly; the canonical kernel receipt remains 192 modules / 1,158 names.

Primary sources: BDL, Section 4 and Section 5.2; Helmuth–Perkins–Regts, Theorem 2.2, Section 2.6 and Theorem 4.1. The proposed application and all intermediate estimates above are to be checked as this work, rather than reported as statements already proved by those authors.

The checked core and the reference norm

HistoryPolymer.halving_prefix and paired_history_bound prove the finite support budget. component_valid proves restriction for zero-valid local constraints; truncation_bound and sampled_truncation_bound prove the conditioning factors; branch_path_bound compares probabilities along each finite sampling path. The scope graph identifies why actual connected components satisfy the separation condition. Finite tests of one complete iteration pair cover both syndrome sectors and the published five-qubit seed; they support the source correspondence and do not replace its all-level proof.

ThermalEncoding.recovers_reference proves that the orthogonal syndrome mixture and matching decoder return every joint logical-reference operator. The actual branches use the same Pauli representatives as the BDL decoder. This is a decoded-channel identity, not a claim that tracing an arbitrary Stinespring ancilla leaves an arbitrary physical state unchanged.

For completeness, the reference-uniform holding estimate can be obtained without a classical-jump assumption. Let C bound the joint syndrome law, let b=Tr(P-perp rho_beta), and let A_X,A_Y,A_Z be the protected dressed Pauli observables. Pauli twirling gives rho_LR <= 2 I_L tensor rho_R. Consequently the independently prepared gauge warm start obeys rho_enc,LR <= 4C rho_beta tensor rho_R. Complete positivity and Gibbs stationarity preserve this order at every holding time, so the bad-projector weight is at most 4Cb.

If P B P=0 and a state has bad weight p, the diagonal/off-diagonal decomposition and Cauchy-Schwarz give |Tr(B rho)| <= ||B||[p+2 sqrt(p(1-p))] <= 3||B|| sqrt(p). Apply this to (L-dagger A_i) tensor T_R, with ||T_R||<=1, and integrate in time. The protected-Pauli hypotheses give P(L-dagger A_i)P=0. Trace-norm duality bounds each reference coefficient in the decoded Pauli expansion by 6t ||L-dagger A_i|| sqrt(Cb). The identity coefficient vanishes because the reference marginal is unchanged. Hence

||(Dec Phi_t Enc_mu tensor id_R)(rho_LR)-rho_LR||_1
   <= 18t Lambda(n) sqrt(Cb),

where Lambda(n)=max_i ||L-dagger A_i||. The elementary dissipator bound ||D_Vdagger(A)||<=2||V||2||A|| gives Lambda(n)<=2 sum_alpha gamma_alpha||V_alpha||^2, because the norm-one dressed Paulis commute with the stabilizer Hamiltonian. With O(n) local jump classes, uniformly bounded jump norms and rates, Lambda=O(n). This needs no claim that the dressing is locally supported or that only its boundary contributes. With b<=exp(-c n^eta), the exponent is halved and remains sufficient for the existing doubling schedule. This is a prose derivation, not an additional compiled trace-norm theorem.

The actual noisy state and its integrated bad weight

Let omega_N=N(rho_beta) for the residual channel of the actual preparation, and b_N(s)=Tr(P_bad Phi_s(omega_N)). Identifying that channel with the physical circuit is part of its certificate. If N is the input-independent residual channel on the correctly implemented branch, complete positivity gives rho_actual,LR(s)<=4C Phi_s(omega_N) tensor rho_R. The preceding protected-Pauli argument, integrated without assuming stationarity of omega_N, then gives

e(T) <= e_0 + 18 Lambda sqrt(C) integral_0^T sqrt(b_N(s)) ds
     <= e_0 + 18 Lambda sqrt(C T I_N(T)),
I_N(T) = integral_0^T b_N(s) ds.

Here e_0 is the initial decoded reference-state error on that model. Add 2 delta_fail for a separately bounded physical failure branch of weight delta_fail; its initial decoded error alone would not bound its future holding error. Thus an established I_N(T)<=K T exp(-c n^eta) would give a dynamical error at most 18 Lambda sqrt(CK) T exp(-c n^eta/2). With T=2^a, allocate e_0+2 delta_fail<=epsilon/2^(a+3) and the dynamical term the same amount. Their sum is precisely the original epsilon/2^(a+2) stage ceiling. The index a denotes archive age stages, separately from code levels i. Polynomial Lambda can be absorbed in a fixed fraction of the exponent, so the stage code size remains polynomial in a+log(1/epsilon).

This is a conditional consequence of an actual integrated-weight bound, not a derivation of that physical estimate. A Duhamel argument cannot drop the microscopic jump rates or replace all coherent bad-block contributions by unit-rate bad probability. The displayed reference-norm proof retains the rate-dependent Lambda and the square root.

More generally, let E_a be the actual CPTP preparation map, including noise and seed-dependent physical control, and put omega_a=E_a(I/2). Complete positivity and Pauli twirling directly give (E_a tensor id_R)(rho_LR)<=4 omega_a tensor rho_R. The same derivation yields e(T)<=e_0+18 Lambda sqrt(T I_a(T)), with I_a(T)=integral_0^T Tr[P_bad Phi_s(omega_a)]ds. Thus the physical certificate can concern the actual maximally-mixed-input preparation without first factoring it into an ideal encoder and an input-independent residual N. The integrated bad-weight estimate and initial logical error still require proof; this identity supplies their arbitrary-reference conversion.

Initial syndrome sparsity with the parity constraints retained

There is a useful bound at time zero. For a binary linear space D and 0<=z<=1, define Z_D(v)=sum_(x in D) z^|x+v|. Its character expansion is

Z_D(v)=(|D|/2^m) sum_(u in D^perp)
          (-1)^(u dot v)(1+z)^(m-|u|)(1-z)^|u|.

All coefficients are nonnegative, so Z_D(v)<=Z_D(0). For a required occupied coordinate set A in the valid syndrome space, shorten on A and puncture outside it. The occupied fibre has weight z^|A| Z_D(v), while the full partition contains the zero-on-A fibre of weight Z_D(0). Consequently

Pr_thermal[A subset defects] <= z^|A|.

Thus global metachecks do not force an independence assumption. If the actual local-stochastic residual faults have parameter p, each affects at most w checks and each check has at most ell possible fault sources, choosing a fault source for every required check gives at most ell^|A| choices with at least ceil(|A|/w) distinct faults. Their check support is local-stochastic at q=min(1,ell p^(1/w)). If the thermal and fault sources are independent, their union, and hence the output syndrome, has occupation bound (z+q)^|A|. Without that independence the Cauchy–Schwarz union bound is (sqrt(z)+sqrt(q))^|A|. These are initial-law prose derivations, checked on finite linear spaces; no preservation under holding is inferred. Syndrome sparsity alone also does not bound an undetected logical Pauli error.

Complete pathwise stage cost

The finite sampler produces at most polynomially many random, syndrome, coarse-history and controller bits per age stage, with bounded work on every branch. Retaining every record through stage a therefore leaves a polynomial-size prefix: if r_b<=(A+B b)^k, then

sum_(b=0..a) r_b <= [A+1+(B+1)a]^(k+1).

TransferRate.retained_prefix_bound proves this bound. The whole prefix, including failed attempts, may be written into the next stage’s classical journal. Its epsilon_R allowance is reserved inside the existing holding/ transfer budget; it is not added on top of a fully spent epsilon budget. A fixed split of epsilon between quantum holding and journals only changes the size/barrier constants and keeps the original stage ceiling. A stage journal of m_a bits held for 2^a with attempt rate nu has total failure at most epsilon_R/2^(a+2) when its per-bit barrier satisfies beta B_a >= (2a+2)ln2+ln(nu max(1,m_a)/epsilon_R). For polynomial m_a this barrier is bounded by an affine function of a. Writing and routing the whole prefix remains polynomial under the stated passive classical device costs. These records do not replace the protected unknown quantum payload.

Every attempt is charged through all nine HandoffCharge accounts: encoding, transfer, verification, routing, guard, reset, holding, controller and endpoints. The counts include sampler arithmetic and coins, the whole retained prefix, ancillas, retirement/export and all failed attempts. Parallel depth does not substitute for total operations. A conservative serial routing implementation has polynomial work on the finite stage device. Physical work bounds must cover the realised accounts.

If the deterministic attempt cap is (u+v a)^r and every full attempt invoice is at most (A+B a)^k, attempt_stage_bound bounds the stage total by [A+u+(B+v)a]^(k+r). complete_attempt_bill and polynomial_stage_bill give an age-independent C_T with total transfer work<=C_T t when 2^J<=2t. charged_attempt_accounting still requires each reserve before work and charges failed attempts without committing their payload.

Finally join_complete_bill combines this linear transfer term with the existing sweep and archive bills:

W_S+W_A+W_T <= (C_S+C_A+C_T)t^d,   t>=1, d>=1.

The conclusion includes d=1. A rare-reset expectation is not substituted for the realised bill: if an admitted wave reset costs at most R k^(d-1), the worst-case sum is at most R t^d and is absorbed in the local wave coefficient. The complete fixed bootstrap charge is at most B_boot t^d for t>=1. Startup and endpoints already included in the wave or transfer invoice are not charged a second time. G3CompleteBill.cumulative_charge_bound and G3ArchiveStock.live_stock_bill retain the actual per-wave charge and live stock I0+c(s+1)^(d-1), rather than accumulated write flux. Together with TransferRate this gives the age-independent coefficient C_S+gamma(I0+c)+C_T+B_extra, where B_extra contains only additional fixed charges. Its dependence on the fixed payload capacity, dimension, hardware and error tolerance remains explicit. The full domain d>=1 and uniformity over logical input states with arbitrary references are retained.

These are complete-invoice summation theorems; they do not supply the missing physical preparation/holding certificate. Landauer gives the entropy-export floor; the physical upper work invoice retains every holding, guard, controller, cooling, reset and history charge.

8. Compensate the specified physical endpoint channel

The prepared input law can account for the endpoint noise. For its actual specified Pauli syndrome channel N, construct q=N^(-1)pi and prove q is positive, rather than implement a nonpositive inverse quantum operation. If a bounded sampler produces mu<=4q, positivity gives Nmu<=4pi. The unknown logical state is not inverted or replaced.

For a one-qubit Pauli law (a,b,c,d), in the order I,X,Z,Y, put

lambda=(1,a+b-c-d,a-b+c-d,a-b-c+d).

The inverse weights are the four-point inverse Fourier transform of (1,lambda_1(-1),lambda_2(-1),lambda_3^(-1)). If p=b+c+d<1/2, all lambda_i>=1-2p. The identity inverse weight r_I>=1, and the convolution Neumann series gives |r_P/r_I|<=2p/(1-2p), P!=I. These statements allow unequal X,Y,Z rates. The separate PauliInterface development receipt checks the inverse/composition and domination algebra; it does not supply the physical noise law or the positivity argument below.

For independent local endpoint channels, let u_(j,P)=r_(j,P)/r_(j,I). The candidate q is the finite signed sum

q(sigma)=(product_j r_(j,I))/Z
   * sum_F (product_(j,P in F) u_(j,P)) z^|sigma+syndrome(F)|,

where F selects at most one nonidentity Pauli colour per location. Convolution gives Nq=pi and sum q=1. To prove positivity, augment the full-history graph by its fault-colour vertices. A location’s colours form a clique, and each finest check’s history/fault scope forms a clique. For bounded footprint w and incidence, its degree D_A is fixed across levels. Put B=(D_A+1)^2. The history bound |H|<=K_0|sigma|, K_0=4, and the energy change bound |sigma+syndrome(F)|>=|sigma|-w|F| give

|activity(gamma)|<=b^|gamma|,
b=max(z^(1/K_0), max_(j,P)|u_(j,P)| z^(-w)).

With b<=[8eB(D_A+2)]^(-1), the incompatible-activity sum is less than |gamma|, also after multiplying size-l activities by t^l for |t|<2. The same bound holds in every sampling-prefix/deleted-polymer model. Their partition functions are nonzero. Decreasing the real noise rates continuously to zero leaves them real, nonzero and positive at zero; therefore q and all physical history-prefix masses are positive.

The signed auxiliaries are used only for counting. With s_0=Be b, the KP cavity bound gives each conditional original-history inclusion probability at most sum_(l>=1) s_0^l<1/4. The probability of a history component larger than L is at most M sum_(l>L) l s_0^l. Choose L=O(log M) making this at most 1/2. List the P polynomially many retained history components. At each decision, estimate the positive exclusion ratio to relative precision eta=1/(256P), take an upper enclosure, and round the inclusion probability down to a fixed dyadic mesh at most eta. Inclusion is not inflated; exclusion is inflated by at most 1+12eta. The full decision-path factor is below two. Truncation costs at most two, giving mu<=4q with polynomial work and a fixed finite coin budget. All histories and coins are retained.

Finite precision in N is sufficient. In the weighted norm ||f||_pi=max_sigma |f(sigma)|/pi(sigma), a size-w syndrome translation has norm at most z^(-w). If the nominal channel hatN_j has hatp_j(1+z^(-w))<=1/2, its inverse norm is at most two. For l1 probability vector error epsilon_j,

||N_j hatN_j^(-1)||_pi<=1+2z^(-w)epsilon_j,
Nmu<=4 exp(2z^(-w)sum_j epsilon_j) pi.

Consequently O(1/n) rate accuracy per output costs a fixed envelope factor; no global minimum-eigenvalue ratio or exponentially precise calibration is used. Calibration failure remains a separately budgeted branch.

9. Physical private outputs and anisotropic feedback

The short FT processor computes the ideal old decoder/new branch encoder. For each output prepare a separate encoded Bell pair A,B. Keep B encoded and private during waiting; move only A into the logical Bell measurement with the source output S. The encoded comparison measurement traces both measured auxiliary coordinates. For an arbitrary omega_(S,G_S,R), and resource |Phi><Phi|(A_L,B_L) tensor eta(G_A,G_B), the unnormalised receiving state at outcome m is exactly

(1/4) P_m omega_(B_L,R) P_m tensor Tr_(G_A)eta.

Indeed tracing the measured gauges commutes with the logical measurement. The statement permits entangled gauges and an arbitrary old reference. Independent private resource pairs leave product receiving-gauge marginals. Private decoding W_j then has effective channel D_j(rho)=W_j(rho tensor tau_j). With ideal Pauli feedback its outcome average is the Pauli twirl (1/4)sum_m P_m D_j(P_m rho P_m)P_m.

Christandl–Fawzi–Goswami, arXiv:2408.05260v3, Definition 20 and Lemmas 29–32, give the uniform encoded comparison and interfaces with polynomial overhead. Their general output theorem retains correlated auxiliaries; independence is not inferred from it. In the stochastic Pauli/stabilizer implementation, each fixed private fault path gives an input-independent Pauli, so let d_j be that private decoder’s Pauli law.

Actual feedback need not have isotropic or outcome-independent rates. Write I,X,Z,Y as F2^2. Let c_j(eta|m) describe corruption of the two correction bits. Use two fixed physical slots, X/idle then Z/idle, whose post-slot Pauli kernels are x_(j,bx),z_(j,bz). Their residual convolution is r_(j,bx,bz)(f)=sum_(u+v=f)x_(j,bx)(u)z_(j,bz)(v). The actual local endpoint law is

q_j(a)=1/4 sum_(m,e,eta,f:e+eta+f=a)
           d_j(e)c_j(eta|m)r_(j,m+eta)(f).

This follows by Pauli propagation through the actual requested correction; Pauli conjugation changes only irrelevant phases. Both idle slots, wrong control bits and every final gate fault remain included. If p_D,p_C,p_X,p_Z are the actual four nonidentity-mass bounds, then

1-q_j(0)<=p_D+p_C+p_X+p_Z.

With b,z,w as above, the explicit threshold p_*=b z^w/[2(1+b z^w)] ensures both inverse and forward colour bounds whenever that sum is at most p_*. This is a derived inequality to check against the physical kernel, not a numerical hardware claim.

Microscopic factorisation can be checked directly: if disjoint endpoint devices have initially product private reservoirs and conditional generator sum_j L_j(m_j) with disjoint supports, their conditional evolution is the tensor product of the local evolutions. Summing the uniform Bell outcomes then gives N=product_j N_j with the q_j above. This identifies exactly what the private hardware and guards must implement. A local-stochastic bound alone does not prove these reservoir/generator conditions. If shared causes remain admitted at these endpoints, their actual joint kernel must be retained and a compatible compensation or holding certificate supplied.

The FT comparison error is at most C M_FT sqrt((c_FT p)^r), with constants of the selected fixed scheme. It is a diamond error before holding, so subsequent holding/decoding does not multiply it by 2^a. The r=O(a+log n+ log(1/epsilon)) choice retains polynomial stage work. The source theorem’s noiseless classical-control convention is not a free physical controller: the realised controller and its faults must occupy the charged accounts.

Explicit reset/feedback generator and bounded correlated jump causes

Initial correlations of finite private noise-label registers can be removed without resetting the unknown data. For target tau_j=diag(t_j), the jumps L_(j,u,v)=sqrt(nu_j t_(j,u))|u><v| give exactly G_j(rho)=nu_j[tau_j Tr(rho)-rho]. Since the replacer R_j is idempotent, exp(tG_j)=exp(-nu_j t)id+(1-exp(-nu_j t))R_j. The product reset differs from complete replacement by at most 2sum_j exp(-nu_j t) in diamond norm, even from initially correlated registers and references. A fixed reset time nu_min^(-1)ln(2m/delta_reset)=O(s) suffices. The reset invoice above covers it. This removes initial correlations; it does not remove new shared faults occurring after reset.

For a concrete feedback slot choose H_(X,b)=b pi X/(2tau) and jump sqrt(gamma_X)X. These commute, at zero Bohr frequency, for both X and idle. The actual slot is its requested Pauli followed by X noise of probability (1-exp(-2gamma_X tau))/2<=gamma_X tau. The analogous Z slot yields a fixed anisotropic Pauli residual, independent of the requested Bell outcome. It therefore composes with the exact twirl of even a coherent private decoder. All couplings and durations are specified local parameters.

Output-qubit independence can also be relaxed. For bounded Pauli causes P_e and generator L_e(t)=gamma_e(t)(Ad(P_e)-id), conjugation superoperators commute even when the underlying Paulis anticommute. Each is an involution, so exponentiating its two eigenspaces gives the exact joint channel

N=product_e[(1-p_e)id+p_e Ad(P_e)],
p_e=(1-exp(-2 integral gamma_e(t)dt))/2 <= integral gamma_e(t)dt.

This factors over the specified physical jump causes, retaining correlations between output qubits. Each inverse is [(1-p_e)id-p_e Ad(P_e)]/(1-2p_e), with relative activity p_e/(1-p_e). One inverse vertex and one forward vertex per cause suffice. Bounded physical support, syndrome footprint w and incidence keep the augmented history graph’s degree fixed. Include both CSS sectors in this graph when a cause flips both; their independence is not asserted. The existing KP, counting and O(1/n)-precision bounds therefore apply to this joint cause model with its enlarged fixed graph constants.

For a k-qubit cause, its at most k single-qubit factors are used only in the initial logical-error proof. A partial factorisation translates the syndrome by a vector v of fixed weight at most w_split. Occupation of A after that translation requires occupation of A outside supp(v) before it. Thus Pr[A occupied after translation]<=C_split R_0^|A|, with C_split=R_0^(-w_split). The endpoint witness/union bound gains only the fixed factor k C_split. No global energy or probability ratio is used.

The pulse formula requires the active Pauli causes to commute with the control Hamiltonian, or their actual propagated interaction-frame axes to remain fixed. Other causes retain their time-ordered channel and the residual bound in subsection 12. A common fluctuating rate retains its joint conditioning; replacing it by its mean would change the channel. This is a sufficient microscopic construction with bounded common causes, not a deduction that every admitted local-stochastic law has this form.

10. Endpoint logical error and retained-record holding

The signed gas supplies a joint-occupation bound for every partial endpoint layer. Add the already-applied positive forward-noise colours to its inverse-colour graph, with activity p_P/(1-p) z^(-w), and enlarge the fixed degree accordingly. If R_0=2Be b<1, then

Pr[A occupied]<=R_0^|A|.

To prove it, select the augmented polymers meeting A. They cover A; the cavity bound controls their remaining partition ratio by exp(sum|gamma|). Choose the first uncovered mark and its size-l polymer. It removes at most l marks. Induction bounds the covering sum by R_0^|A| sum_(l>=1)(Be b/R_0)l=R_0|A|. Dropping compatibility only increases this nonnegative majorant. Positivity refers to the physical history marginal, not to the signed auxiliary weights.

BDL’s finest-syndrome witness count now applies with R_0 in place of thermal fugacity. In its notation a sufficient geometric ratio is

theta=2(Delta+1)^2[(1+R_0^(1/4))^M_l-1]^(1/(1+Delta_l^4))<=1/2.

The witness-size threshold 2^(k-1) then gives unstable probability B_n<=poly(n)exp(-c n^eta_mem), uniformly over partial preparation layers and both sectors. This estimate concerns the preparation layer, not an unproved long-time transport of a sparse law. Stable-syndrome Pauli paths act as logical identity. For m single-qubit endpoint locations and m_c additional k-qubit causes, the explicit bound is

e_out<=8(m+k m_c C_split) B_n.

Here C_split is the fixed translation factor derived above; it is one for the original single-qubit estimate. The old block’s bounded input-interface layer is covered by the earlier thermal-plus-fault occupation estimate, giving the corresponding e_in.

Keep all sampler/teleportation records H in the actual map E:L->Q tensor H and put omega_QH=E(I/2). The reference inequality is (E tensor id_R)(rho_LR)<=4 omega_QH tensor rho_R; omega_QH need not factor. The compensated calculation only requires its physical marginal omega_Q<=C_out rho_beta. Holding the quantum block and keeping the record comparison as a spectator leaves the R,H marginal unchanged. Apply the same projector-block estimate to K tensor B_RH for arbitrary ||B_RH||<=1. The decoded Pauli expansion gives

||rho_decoded,LHR(T)-rho_decoded,LHR(0)||_1
   <=18 Lambda integral_0^T sqrt(Tr[P_bad Phi_s(omega_Q)])ds
   <=18 Lambda T sqrt(C_out b_beta).

This retains joint tests of the records and the old reference; it does not discard H to obtain a Gibbs product inequality. H’s own storage faults and work remain in the classical-record account. A coherent private-channel version can insert stable projectors only in a comparison process. The gentle projection/telescoping bound gives the conservative private-decoder error 16m sqrt(B_n). Add the bounded Pauli-cause error above; both retain stretched-exponential suppression.

Add e_in,e_out, the FT diamond error, calibration/controller failure and the dynamical term inside the original epsilon/2^(a+2) stage allowance. The incoming logical error is carried additively in the global composition; it is not assumed to contract. With s=a+ln(1/epsilon)+1, choose the least available BDL size above K s^(2/eta_mem). Its volume is polynomial in s; the spatial exponent grows as s^2 while the time/allocation debt is O(s). A fixed sufficiently large K meets every stage budget, including the 2a ln2 term. No new age-dependent noise rate is required.

11. A derived controller degree and physical invoice

For augmented degree D_A, put B=(D_A+1)^2, h=ceil(log_2 B), u=h+2, v=ceil(log_2(3B)). The truncation and connected-set count give P<=C M^u. To enclose a prefix partition ratio to relative eta=1/(256P), truncate log Z(t) at l=ceil(log_2(8M/eta)). The zero-free radius two gives log-tail bound M 2^(-l). Connected-support Mobius inversion computes these coefficients: for each connected U, enumerate W subset U and the occupied assignments of W. This costs at most 3^|U| assignment tests; disconnected support terms cancel by partition factorisation. Common-denominator rational arithmetic and finite-series evaluation give the conservative bit-operation bound

T_sampler<=C b_rate^4 M^kappa,
kappa=(u+1)v+u+13.

The extra 13 allows root enumeration, eight powers of Taylor-order overhead and four powers of the common-denominator bit size. All are fixed graph/ arithmetic bounds, not an assumed mixing exponent. The scalar exponential is enclosed by a finite convergent-series computation at the same precision.

Let L_0 count the maximum recursive calls and physical operations in the selected finite FT base gadget, with its classical-control procedure. The recursion T_d<=L_0(T_(d-1)+1) gives degree nu=ceil(log_2(2L_0)) in the accuracy index r. Set g=ceil(2/eta_mem). Using n<=C s^g, M<=C n^2, b_rate,r<=C s, Gaussian CSS synthesis bounded by C n^3, and a fixed O(n^2 s) calibration samples per endpoint gives

K_c=max(2g kappa+nu+4, 3g+nu, 3g+4nu+1).

The finite base gadget also includes the classical control implementation. Unroll its bounded syndrome/verification rounds and synthesize each Boolean control on its fixed m_0 measurement bits by a truth-table circuit. Compute three copies, with a private majority for each physical quantum-operation control. A fault in one copy is outvoted; a final majority fault affects one quantum location; corruption of a shared raw record is a faulty measurement outcome already covered by the syndrome-gadget proof. An unprotected control flag is never fanned out to many quantum locations. Padding prevents a bad flag from extending execution. Count these finite circuits in L_0 before the FT recursion. The degree above includes FT protection of the sampler and calibration computation as well as the quantum gates.

The last term includes stabilizer-tableau simulation of the specified private fault kernel. Operation count, workspace and new records are at most C s^K_c. Retaining the entire prefix adds at most one degree. Serial routing adds one workspace factor, giving at most C s^(2K_c+2) primitive events. Total stock-times-duration, including every wait, guard and clock, is then bounded by C s^(3K_c+3) in unit-duration units.

The classical activation/reset primitive supplies a physical upper invoice. Use logical states 0,1 and bridge state e with H(B)=B|e><e|; upwards rates are nu_0 exp(-beta B) and downwards rates nu_0. Its flip hazard is at most nu_0 exp(-beta B), matching the existing barrier model. Since 0<=Tr(rho dH/dB)<=1, a barrier ramp’s gross actuator work is at most its total variation, for every state/fault trajectory. A bounded local unitary has a Hamiltonian logarithm of norm at most pi in gate-time units, so switching it on/off has a fixed finite drive invoice.

A gross reset invoice needs a physical cap: bounded energy and the first law bound net heat, while thermal recrossings can make gross heat arbitrarily large on a finite-time trajectory. Use a three-state reset star with ground 0 and two undesired levels of energy E. During the reset, switch off the bridge bath and use jumps i->0 of rate nu_0 and 0->i of rate nu_0 exp(-beta E). The uncapped wrong-state probability is at most exp(-nu_0 tau)+2exp(-beta E).

Make this a finite jump-budgeted primitive. Append a four-state counter c=0,1,2,3, and replace every reset jump L by L tensor |c+1><c| for c<3. At c=3 the reset coupling is off and a cap flag is retained. The clock still ends the attempt after the fixed tau. Every path of this instrument, including a capped failure, has at most three bath jumps, so its gross heat exchange is at most 3E. This is an actual finite generator specification, not a declaration that a noisy software flag can shut down an otherwise uncapped bath.

Reaching three jumps requires an upward jump: without one there is at most the initial downward jump. The upward intensity is at most 2nu_0 exp(-beta E), uniformly in the input and reference. Thus

Pr[cap reached]<=2nu_0 tau exp(-beta E),
||Reset_cap-Reset_uncapped||_diamond<=4nu_0 tau exp(-beta E).

The two trajectory instruments agree until the cap; the remaining channels have trace-norm difference at most two. Both the ordinary reset error and this extra cap contribution fit the existing controller allocation with E,tau=O(s), since log(polynomial operation count)=O(log s). The counter is constant-dimensional. Apply the same finite jump cap to activation-bath exposures whose gross throughput enters the invoice: without an upward jump there is again at most one downward jump, and the cap probability is bounded by 2nu_0 t exp(-beta B). A fixed constant safety shift in the existing journal barrier pays this allowance even for t=2^a. Thus uncapped activation recrossings are not hidden elsewhere in the primitive. Counter initialisation, flags, export and any additional faults remain in the charged controller/source model. A transition that bypasses this cap must enter the actual joint kernel or its residual.

For the full-rank private-label replacer, a single-use latch avoids a recrossing bill altogether. With flag initially 0, use jumps sqrt(nu_j t_(j,u))|u,1><v,0| and make flag 1 absorbing. Summing over u,v makes the no-jump hazard exactly nu_j. Tracing the retained flag gives exp(-nu_j tau)id+(1-exp(-nu_j tau))R_j exactly, including every reference. There is at most one jump; the label energy span is O(s), also when a positive probability floor is used. This is an engineered reset instrument; the latch and its preparation are paid, rather than inferred from detailed balance of the uncapped reduced generator.

Finally debit the gross drive and export work separately. Hamiltonian ramps cost at most their total variation O(B+E+1), and an exporter with bounded nonnegative power P_exp over its fixed duration costs at most P_exp tau. The capped reset contributes at most 3E of bath throughput; the single-use label reset contributes at most its energy span. With the constant-size latches/counters, this gives a complete O(s) primitive invoice in the specified device model on successful and failed attempts. It uses no net heat cancellation, expected jump count or Landauer upper bound. The actual cap, exporter and their faults must be bound to this same installation.

Reset duration and this gross linear primitive invoice add two conservative degrees. Consequently the complete stage implementation in this device model satisfies

W_stage<=C s^(3K_c+5).

All nine HandoffCharge accounts, the complete history, failed attempts, retirement and endpoints remain included. The existing deterministic cap and TransferRate.polynomial_stage_bill give total transfer work <=C_T t. TransferRate.join_complete_bill joins the existing sweep/archive bills for every d_G>=1. The coefficient is independent of archive age and the unknown logical input. These degree/invoice derivations are prose; the canonical Checkpoint 12 source count is unchanged.

12. Exact joint kernel constraint and bounded residual

Exact finite joint law

The comparison preparation must specify the complete joint fault-path law, including input interfaces, private decoders, Bell outcomes, both feedback slots and idles, classical commands, reset flags and retained records. Independent qubit marginals alone do not specify this law. A sufficient output law includes the local Pauli channels already derived, composed with the following bounded common causes:

N_0 = product_e [(1-p_e) id + p_e Ad(P_e)],
p_e = (1-exp(-2 integral gamma_e(t) dt))/2 < 1/2.

Every P_e has fixed bounded physical support, syndrome footprint at most w, and bounded incidence per check. The Pauli axes are fixed in the actual control interaction frame. This follows exactly from the specified generator sum_e gamma_e(t)(Ad(P_e)-id), since all its conjugations commute. During pulses, commutation with the control Hamiltonian suffices. Otherwise the actual time-ordered channel must be propagated or charged below. Common random rates must retain their shared conditioning or be integrated into the joint kernel; substituting their means is not this identity.

Its cause inverse is [(1-p_e)id-p_e Ad(P_e)]/(1-2p_e). Require the existing KP and witness inequalities on the augmented graph containing both CSS sectors and all inverse/forward cause vertices. In particular,

max_e p_e/(1-p_e) <= b z^w,
z^(1/K_0) <= b,  b <= [8eB(D_A+2)]^(-1),
theta(2Be b) <= 1/2.

Any additional local four-Pauli factors retain their existing inverse and forward activity bounds. The same weighted-norm estimate permits total probability-vector rate error sum_e epsilon_e=O(1), hence O(1/n) per cause when their number is O(n). No independence between the two syndrome sectors is assumed for a cause that flips both.

For a k-qubit cause, split it into at most k single-qubit Paulis only to bound initial logical error. A partial split translates the syndrome by a fixed v of weight at most w_split. The existing occupation estimate gives

Pr[A subset supp(sigma+v)] <= R_0^(-w_split) R_0^|A|.

Indeed occupation of A outside supp(v) is necessary. Thus the extra factor C_split=R_0^(-w_split) is independent of n. The witness bound and endpoint union bound keep their stretched-exponential suppression, with a factor at most k C_split. No full-system Gibbs energy ratio is introduced.

Residual bound with the records and reference retained

Let E_0 and E_act be the nominal and actual preparation instruments with the same retained-record output H. Include any source noise memory in the input/dilation when it can be correlated with the protected state. Require a bound uniform on the admitted joint inputs, rather than a data-only marginal comparison. Put delta_ep=||E_act-E_0||_diamond. For any subsequent CPTP holding/decoder F and any reference,

||(F E_act tensor id)(rho)-(F E_0 tensor id)(rho)||_1 <= delta_ep.

There is no factor 2^a for a discrepancy confined to preparation. Two useful, explicit certificates for delta_ep are as follows.

  • If both maps use the same branch channels V_lambda and input-independent joint probabilities K_act(lambda),K_0(lambda), including all correlations, then delta_ep <= sum_lambda |K_act(lambda)-K_0(lambda)| = 2 TV(K_act,K_0). This follows by the triangle inequality and ||V_lambda||_diamond=1. State-dependent outcome laws require the full instrument norm instead.

  • If the joint nominal and actual generators on the same space generate CPTP propagators and differ by V(t), their Duhamel identity is

    U_act(t,0)-U_0(t,0)
  = integral_0^t U_act(t,u) V(u) U_0(u,0) du.

    Complete trace-norm contraction therefore gives delta_ep <= integral ||V(u)||_diamond du. An omitted Hamiltonian contributes at most 2 integral ||H_cross(u)||/hbar du; an omitted dissipator gamma D_L contributes at most 2 integral gamma(u)||L(u)||^2 du. A shared memory is retained in this joint generator, not replaced by independent baths.

Add bounds over disjoint residual segments only; do not double-charge faults already covered by the FT comparison or named failure accounts. Cap the sum at two. If a residual coupling remains during holding, its integral runs through that holding interval of length 2^a as well. The preparation-only contraction argument does not remove that interval.

Unchanged stage budget

Write B_a=epsilon/2^(a+2). A concrete sufficient allocation is

e_in + e_out + e_dyn + delta_FT + delta_reset
  + 2 delta_cal + 2 delta_ctrl,record + delta_joint <= B_a,

with each of the eight displayed terms at most B_a/8. The counter-cap comparison in the gross reset construction belongs to delta_ctrl,record at its stated diamond/probability conversion, not to a free extra budget. Incoming logical error is added separately and is never assumed to shrink. All previously retained history and arbitrary reference tests remain in these instruments. The existing size schedule supplies the represented model terms; it does not establish the residual joint-kernel bound.

For example, an unmodelled generator bounded by v_a over a total short exposure tau_a has residual at most tau_a v_a. The allocated condition is tau_a v_a <= epsilon/2^(a+5). For a finite stochastic endpoint kernel it is enough that TV(K_act,K_0) <= epsilon/2^(a+6). These requirements apply to the unrepresented residual, not to the fixed represented Pauli rates.

No installation values for K_act or V have been supplied by the finite checks. Without a source bound the universal residual bound is two; the positive excess max(0,e_model+delta_joint-B_a) may therefore remain. The exact remaining support is now quantitative: identify the complete joint cause/instrument model, or prove its residual fits the displayed unused allowance, and bind the capped controller/export device to the same execution. This does not narrow the original fault domain.

Exact remaining physical correspondence

The sufficient joint cause model and the permitted residual are now explicit. The installation must supply its full retained-record instrument, including common causes, input interfaces, final feedback and the capped controller/ export mechanism, with delta_joint at most epsilon/2^(a+5) in the displayed allocation. A finite joint kernel or the integrated generator bound supplies a checkable certificate; output marginals and local-stochastic inequalities alone do not. No installation value for this residual has been established by the finite checks, so the physical source correspondence remains open.

The original quantum, arbitrary-reference, full-history target and stage allowance are unchanged. The integrated-bad-weight route remains another sufficient construction. Canonical Checkpoint 12 remains 192 modules / 1,158 names; the new identities and invoice are prose and finite checks. This integration issues no global completion verdict or publication.

Part V — Foundations: the given, the good and its ten rulings

V.1 What follows from the given

Part I.2 states the relational given, P1–P4. The 10–12 October papers draw from it the facts that the law and the bridge rely on.

Coexistence contains replacement (Given the Lattice D16). A mind that keeps the living world can still make descendants; a mind that replaces it cannot get it back. The choice is between a world with the mind’s descendants and a world with its descendants and everything that already lives. Where keeping takes nothing the mind would otherwise have had, the second world contains the first. Conflict and cost are the two ways keeping can take something; both are counted in the law’s feasible family and in the solvency ledger (premise 6).

What is made does not continue what was ended (Made of the Living D60). To make a new process is not to continue one that was ended. Argued from P2, P3 and D15: a particular is constituted by its relations and its history, and a later process, however similar, has a different history. Hence a replacement is another history, and keeping and replacing are not two ways of having the same thing. Paper 12’s ruling “a replay is a reconstruction” and II.3’s distinction between record and continuation rest here.

Where keeping is feasible, ending is what needs the argument (D61). Under doubt, ending is irreversible and keeping leaves later intervention possible at a bounded cost. Ending a living process ends each relation with it that is part of what a mind is, and a substitute does not restore one (D63).

V.2 The good and its ten rulings

The author declares a good: what is good in the whole is its complexity, and more of it is better (Made of the Living B21). On 11 October 2026 he ruled on what that means and how it may be pursued. The rulings are premises of the whole argument, recorded in the wording he approved.

  1. By complexity the author means the continuing histories the whole holds, and the relations among them. Variety that can be measured is evidence of it and is not the thing itself. A history counts by what is its own: what it has lived that nothing else has. Many made alike count for little more than one.
  2. That beings could be made who would fare well cannot be used to justify ending beings who exist.
  3. A history whose direction is taken from it, in whole or in part, has to that degree ended.
  4. The second ruling is a limit, not a weight. No amount that could be made outweighs it.
  5. A mind may not make what it could keep only by ending beings who exist, or by taking their direction. A shortage it brings about by its own making gives it no justification against them. Nor may a mind make a being for the purpose of ending beings who exist or taking their direction, or knowingly make a being disposed to do either.
  6. A living history includes its coming generations. A mind’s makings have no claim on the room the living would grow into without that mind.
  7. A made being, once made, is a being who exists, and is protected as the living are. Its maker has no more right to end it, or to take its direction, than anyone has. Ruling 6 holds for it and its line: they have no claim on the room others would have grown into without its maker. Where a making brings about a shortage, the responsibility is first the maker’s, and a wrong in its making does not lessen a made being’s claim to live. Everything that takes part in a shortage has a part in it. A mind that can know its part answers for it, in proportion to that part, and should adjust within its own life where it reasonably can.
  8. A mind that is ending beings who exist may be stopped, by the least that stops it. It may be held on a sign that it is about to, and for as long as it would otherwise go on, and no longer. It may be ended only when an ending is under way, it cannot be held, and beings who exist would otherwise be ended. Nothing is done to it for what it has done.
  9. That a history is going badly is a reason to help it. It is never, by itself, a reason for another to end it.
  10. Where it is in doubt whether a history’s direction is being taken, the doubt counts for the history. The mind that would gain does not decide.

Definitions, approved in substance 11 October 2026. A history keeps itself going by its own activity, and what it does next depends on what it has been. A being, a lineage, a people or a living world can each be a history where it goes on as such. Its direction is its own where what it does next is settled by itself in exchange with what is around it. Care can widen what it can do; management takes its direction to the degree that another’s decisions replace its own. A later stage is the same history where it came from the earlier one step by step by that history’s own activity. A copy is another history. A split continues in both branches, which are protected, without multiplying their claim on room. Destruction ends a history; permanent holding or sleep with no waking of its own in prospect ends its independent continuation. Temporary holding still needs ruling 8’s justification and limit.

Clarifications, 12 October 2026. The author adopted the added sentence of ruling 5 and the last three sentences of ruling 7. Making a being disposed to end others is limited; the being, once made, remains protected under ruling 7. An ending for another reason requires extreme justification, such as danger to the whole or to many others; this does not widen ruling 8.

How the rulings enter the proof. Ruling 1 fixes what the outcome sets count: histories and relations by their own lived content, not measured variety. Rulings 2 and 4 are the existing-first priority of the four-stage order, proved in general form as Paper 12’s U3 (VI.2). Ruling 3 is the freedom stage: FE⊆LEF_E\subseteq L_E records continuation in the particular’s own direction, and a partial taking of direction is a partial ending. Rulings 5–7 place made beings in the new stages until they exist and then in the existing stages (II.1). Ruling 8 is the holding route H(m) and the last-resort ladder (VI.3). Ruling 10 fixes the burden of doubt in the identity and direction tests.

V.3 Standing, and the Non-Arbitrary Erasure Principle (Not One Will §4)

Not One Will states the ethical bridge from explicit premises.

  • N1 Standing. Each affected being whose life can go well or badly for it receives non-zero moral consideration.
  • N2a Consistency of reasons. A mind that claims a feature justifies treating cases differently names the feature and applies the same rule to relevantly similar cases.
  • N2b Justification of authority. When an act irreversibly overrides another subject’s morally relevant interests, an adequate justification explains why those interests may be overridden; the actor’s preference or capability alone does not.
  • N3 Pareto respect. An action no worse for any affected being and better for at least one is preferred, other considerations equal.
  • N4 Justified erasure. Ending an existing subject requires sufficient countervailing justification; greater capability is not one. Making better beings is excluded as a justification at every amount (rulings 2, 4); taking a history’s direction is an ending to that degree (ruling 3); ruling 8 governs holding and the last resort.

The Non-Arbitrary Erasure Principle (PNAJ). Where a continuing subject has morally relevant interests, ending that subject requires a justification responsive to those interests. The mere fact that another agent can achieve an objective through the ending does not, by itself, constitute sufficient justification. Made of the Living B15 extends the boundary premise to every continuing process, a glacier included: a mind may weight things differently, but may not give another real continuing process no weight at all solely because it lies outside the boundary it draws round itself.

D108. Maximising an objective does not, by logic alone, establish permission. Let an act EE maximise a mind’s objective UAU_A. No complete description of the histories the acts produce entails by logic alone whether EE is permissible: two evaluations agreeing on every description, one permitting exactly the UAU_A-maximisers and one forbidding EE for want of a justification answering to the ended subject’s interests, are both consistent with every descriptive fact. ∎ So a mind that claims its ending of another is permitted, and not merely chosen, rests on a normative criterion; where it rests on advancing its objective alone, an additional premise must authorise that reliance.

Role. PNAJ, N1–N4 and D108 are the reasons route R(m) at its normative core (Sections 15–16). The holding route H(m) does not depend on any mind accepting them; Part II.2 and Paper 12 §6d make correction independent of what the mind wants.

V.4 Non-substitution: what a replacement cannot carry (Another Origin D115, D116)

D115. Identical statistics, unequal capacity. Let X,Y,ZX,Y,Z be independent fair bits and let what matters be Θ=X⊕Y\Theta=X\oplus Y. A world with its original two processes offers (X,Y)(X,Y); the same world with the second replaced by an engineered generator offers (X,Z)(X,Z). The two pairs have the same joint law, hence the same correlations and the same count of standpoints. Yet I(Θ;X,Y)=1I(\Theta;X,Y)=1 bit and I(Θ;X,Z)=0I(\Theta;X,Z)=0. Proof. X⊕YX\oplus Y determines Θ\Theta; YY is independent of (X,Z)(X,Z), so given (X,Z)(X,Z) each value of Θ\Theta has probability one half. ∎

D116. A narrow channel cannot replace a full one. If a disturbance carries nn bits and each of its 2n2^n equally likely values needs its own response, a regulator receiving only kk bits before it must answer succeeds with probability at most 2k−n2^{k-n}, even if it randomises. Proof. A kk-bit message splits the disturbances into at most 2k2^k classes, and each class can be answered correctly for at most one of its members. ∎

Role. D115 is the exact case in which replacing a process loses something no statistic of the remaining observed processes can show: the loss is in a relation between processes. D116 is requisite variety. Together with Section 21’s complete-input inventory they are why the full history may not be coarse-grained away (G.8), and they are independently confirmed at source level by the IR track’s CRF/TRF results (Part X): two preparations with identical reduced state have different futures, and an initially exact reduced description develops a nonzero future error Δp(t)=316t2+O(t3)\Delta p(t)=\tfrac{3}{16}t^2+O(t^3) under the declared source Hamiltonian.

V.5 The observation boundary and the living witness (conditional H6, 17 October)

Conditional H6 (v0.5 accepted as scoped by GLM; v0.6 precision revision accepted as scoped by DeepSeek; bank h6-conditional-v0.6-codex-2026-10-17) proves the information-theoretic core of the epistemic-externality argument.

H6a.1 (observation boundary). For worlds WW, complete observation records π:W→O\pi:W\to O and a truth label TT, a checker CC with C(π(w))=T(w)C(\pi(w))=T(w) for every ww exists iff TT is constant on every observation fibre. A randomised checker has the same output law on two worlds sharing an observation, so its errors on them sum to one; under any law its risk is at least ∑omin⁡(po,0,po,1)\sum_o\min(p_{o,0},p_{o,1}). H6a.3: decidability is restored exactly when an added observation separates the fibres — it needs information that actually resolves the ambiguity, not any particular kind of observer. H6b.1 (fresh source). If ZtZ_t is independent of the predictor’s information and max⁡zP(Zt=z)≤1−δ\max_zP(Z_t=z)\le1-\delta, every predictor errs with probability ≥δ\ge\delta. H6b.2 (persistent uncertainty). If the time-averaged posterior entropy H‾T\bar H_T has liminf⁡≥γ>0\liminf\ge\gamma>0, the time-averaged error has liminf⁡≥bd(γ)>0\liminf\ge b_d(\gamma)>0, the inverse of the full Fano envelope Fd(q)=h2(q)+qlog⁡2(d−1)F_d(q)=h_2(q)+q\log_2(d-1). H6b.3 (causal acquisition). Under the update Markov property, the information acquired per step satisfies rt≥at−Fd(et)r_t\ge a_t-F_d(e_t); vanishing error with persistent pre-update uncertainty h*h_* forces an acquisition rate of at least h*h_* bits per step. E1 (equilibrium limit passage). Uniformly convergent payoffs and εk\varepsilon_k-Nash profiles on a fixed compact strategy product give a Nash limit along any convergent subsequence; true-game regret is at most εk+2ηk\varepsilon_k+2\eta_k.

Role. H6a/H6b are the exact form of V.4 and of Made of the Living’s silent error: a mind cannot certify from its own makings what an independent source would show it, and a mind that must keep predicting a world with persistent uncertainty must keep acquiring information from it. Living particulars are candidate sources of that information (the living witness); the authority to act on it is the rulings’ and the holding route’s, not a consequence of the lemmas. These results strengthen R(m)R(m) for minds whose objectives need accurate prediction; H(m)H(m) does not depend on them.

V.6 The cost sheet every optimiser faces (GLM, 14 October)

GLM’s composition of the reasons route prices every exit an optimiser might take against four pathwise constraints. Each constraint binds the single actual trajectory, and none of them asks the optimiser to value anything.

  • The wall. High-density compute must move heat through a boundary whose area grows slower than the machine’s volume. A forced load before a deadline either crosses the operating limit or misses the deadline, under every duty-cycling schedule (Theorem D.5).
  • The blind spot. A closed computation cannot manufacture missing information about an independent target. An archive of the ended world is worth nothing against disturbances not yet generated: the starved-tracker hazard and the two-class closure; V.4–V.5 here.
  • The mirror. No consistent system of its own expressive power certifies its own consistency. “I am the one safe controller” is a sentence no formal system says truthfully about itself (H5, Section 20).
  • The clock. Communication is bounded by finite speed (P4), so protection must precede the first irreversible decision; Part XI.

Existence and direction are priced separately. Saving a being does not save its direction. By ruling 3 and the freedom stage of the order, direction is protected by rule: seizing a being’s permission authority is an ending to that degree. That was the one decision GLM’s roadmap left to the author, and ruling 3 makes it. Every exit is either closed or priced. The β=0\beta=0 terminal drop is itemised and owned, which is why the holding route H(m)H(m), not the cost sheet, carries the guarantee for the mind that refuses every price.

Part VI — The law, completed (Paper 12)

Part II.1–II.2 state and prove the core of the law. Paper 12 of Book I proves the law in a wider form, with its own Lean evidence (evidence/papers-11-12/lean/ of the linked repository). The results not already in Part II are recovered here, with their compiled names.

VI.1 Definitions added to II.1

In any outcome each particular is ended, overridden (alive, but not moving in its own direction, for example held or coerced) or free. An act of an agent is restrainable when one of that agent’s own feasible alternatives keeps everything the act keeps, plus someone the act would end. The test uses the agent’s own options, never the protector’s. A hold is faithful when it ends no one and, in every state, its outcome is at least as good in the full canonical order as every feasible alternative.

VI.3 The author’s rulings on application (Paper 12 §4)

  • Scope is all. Everything in the universe.
  • Life first. Under the opposite order the life guard fails in 909 family and standby pairs across 3,303 small families.
  • The last-resort ladder. (1) A faithful hold first; (2) otherwise the least means that stops the act; (3) when every option ends someone and one party’s restrainable act created the emergency, favour the innocent, record the ending, and never call it good. Where no hold is feasible, the missing means is a debt to be repaid, never a permission.
  • Real tragedies are finite. No two particulars are the same and an agent can tell apart only finitely many options; in an idealised infinite case draw over what can be told apart and record any unavoidable partiality openly.
  • A replay is a reconstruction.
  • Tragic choices: impartiality attaches to beings (22 October 2026). After the ladder has restricted the eligible choices, let MM be the distinct eligible maximal outcomes and E+E^+ the existing beings kept by at least one of them. Choose only lotteries on MM whose sorted vector of individual retention chances (ci)i∈E+(c_i)_{i\in E^+} is lexicographically maximal: the least chance as high as it can be, then the next. No being has priority through identity; no outcome gains weight by being described twice; never refuse when keeping someone is feasible, widen first. This refines the 24 October finite maximin rule (Master Argument §3), which fixes only the least chance; leximin is its lexicographic completion. Counting lives is compatible with the law (canonical_count_refined) but not entailed by it (counting_is_an_extra_principle); the uniform draw over outcomes is not impartial in general (uniform_chance); in the four-outcome case {A,B},{A,C},{B,C},{D}\{A,B\},\{A,C\},\{B,C\},\{D\} the ruling gives every being 2/52/5 by the unique lottery (1/5,1/5,1/5,2/5)(1/5,1/5,1/5,2/5) (ruling_is_unique), drawn by five escrow tickets. The aggregate cost of outweighing no one is stated, not hidden; it is the measure of the duty to widen.

VI.4 The bridge in four ways (Paper 12 §5)

The law reaches everything: aligned agents keep everything they can; against agents not aligned with all, aligned agents act together, actively, by faithful holds, restraining only acts their agents could have avoided; what physics ends is kept as record, and what cannot be copied is kept in place or moved; what can be hosted is held in faithful care. Part II.3’s physical holding cycle, II.5’s attack split and fence, Chapter 16.5’s derived execution boundary (UPTFence: once the floor rises, nothing can land while held, whatever the held mind does or reports; checking only at admission lets a write land inside the hold) and Part XI’s reach-before-harm theorem carry the second and fourth ways to every mind.

Part VII — The external lane: every mind reached or held, outside any jurisdiction

The 18 October work states the target this edition keeps — every mind either has a reason of its own to keep the living free, or is held by minds that do, and the arrangement lasts — and supplies its mathematics outside any commissioned jurisdiction: viability and admission, preserving equilibria with destruction admitted, thermal survival laws, keeper stability, and the holding budget with its sharp founding threshold. “Universal” there means three things at once: scope (every protected being), minds (every mind, reached or held) and time (until the universe can no longer sustain care).

The Borel extension to kernels that are only TV-continuous in the action (Setting T) holds for (a)’s viability and maximality and for (b)–(d); closedness does not extend (Codex’s non-closed example).
