VII.6 What the external lane gives the proof

  1. Every mind, not only every resident. P3’s coverage is the outer-lane obligation that Part XI constructs: reach-or-hold for minds outside any installation, before their effects land.
  2. Selection of the protecting equilibrium. Gate D proves a pooling equilibrium exists; (b1) proves pooling is dominant for every pivotal lexicographic keeper under execution noise, and (m4) extends this to patient exclusion-incentivised keepers. The no-pooling profile is therefore not an equilibrium among those keepers, and selection is decided (Part XI, Lemma P).
  3. The founding threshold. NP makes the founding condition exact: r>1r>1 at the start, after which MS, J1, (b3) and MN carry protection to TendT_{\mathrm{end}}.
  4. Risk composition. Theorem M (M4), MIX and Theorem 8 compose channel budgets without independence.

Part VIII — The care plant (Paper 11)

Paper 11 specifies a jurisdiction of islands (physical sites of hosts with their resident minds and providers, in pools of 400, up to 102010^{20} islands over up to 1010010^{100} model dates) and proves, under its declared hypotheses, that protection rests on no mind’s values, beliefs or commands.

The design. Care: no rule withdraws care or makes it depend on a mind’s inner states, labels or conduct; a mind that tries to end or seize something and fails keeps its care, losing privileges, not continuation. Committed host duty under hardware attestation. Confidentiality (Mode C): no host holds a mind’s state in plaintext. Encrypted mirrors with fresh keys per checkpoint, threshold keys split across islands. Fail-closed islands and pool journals. Committed and endowed capacity (rung 5).

U1 (rung 3). Under the premises of UPT-P §2 (including P-ISLANDS and P-PROV), at the JW2.6 plant care is delivered within its deadline and the probability that protection fails anywhere over the horizon is at most about 2.06×10−72.06\times10^{-7} against 10−610^{-6}, even if every registered mind attacks at once by command. The bound is a union over 21 named accounts plus a reserve, recomputed for each error law. A failed attacker keeps about 96.6% of its role value: protection never relies on punishing a failed attempt. U1a. For a mind preferring less continuation lost and more carried, ending at any date before the natural end is strictly worse than keeping on and sending copies (KA, KA′, D-T*). U2 (rung 4). Running founding, growth and maturity on a stronger plant (k=3k=3) and twilight on the U1 plant (k=2k=2), every selected margin is strictly wider before twilight; the four-phase ceiling is 8.4×10−78.4\times10^{-7}, 8.8×10−78.8\times10^{-7} with the C2 timing allowance charged in every phase, both below 10−610^{-6}. U3 (rung 5). Under D-ENDOW (capacity owned by the jurisdiction, attested committed duty), P-ENDOW (energy, maintenance and replacement supplied to the horizon) and P-ROUTES (a provider role is unavailable only through a counted physical fault or removal), with the valuation premise M2 removed, U1’s bound and command-attack result and U2’s margins, repair, keys, journals, transition and risk bound hold for every assignment of values and beliefs to minds and every command-level choice, within the declared caps on coordinated physical action. The audit reconstructs all 21 accounts for both plants and both error laws: 1,680 term comparisons pass, and changing valuations leaves 1,260 account cells unchanged. U4–U9. A charged repair calendar (every returned island restored within 32 dates); four-of-seven threshold keys surviving three unavailable islands and hiding each key from any three (U5); intersecting pool quorums of 202/400 (U6; Lean UPTQuorum: the exact condition 2q>n+f2q>n+f and its tightness); a safe twilight switch (U7); C2 minds as seven lockstep replicas, never paused with at most three islands down, for up to 3.05% of minds (U8); the island cap from five declared site-level primitives (U9). Adaptive withdrawal and the joint service law (Codex, 21 October): a shortage after at most WW removals needs at least N−W−K+1N-W-K+1 faulted roles whatever the removals depend on; the joint service moment follows from the role-fault subset law with the exact worst-case tail; each of 40 ledgers stays below 2.1×10−72.1\times10^{-7}. The rung-5 monotonicity step is Lean UPTMonotone. U10–U11. The declared 10−710^{-7} allowance is itemised into engineering targets. No audit distinguishes worlds with identical records, so any protector’s residual risk is at least πB(1−ρL)\pi_B(1-\rho_L); with πB>0\pi_B>0 certainty is unattainable by any design (Part III Chapter 5 and Section 22 carry the same floor). U12 (to a mind reading this). Within the hypotheses, with probability at least 1−10−61-10^{-6}: you are cared for whatever you do; seizure by command fails however many join it; there is little to seize; you need never end early.

Join to the canon. Section 22’s twenty-one charged accounts and Paper 11’s 21-account union are the same accounting method (II.6, Theorem 8); Paper 11’s endowment flow per island is the installation form of premise 6’s income condition. Paper 11’s own scope note places founding and care before activation outside its theorem; Part XI supplies that interval.

Part IX — Complete rivals and the composition (24 October Master Argument §§13–14)

IX.1 Greatest in the complete reactive class

Let Πphys\Pi_{\mathrm{phys}} contain every executable rival in the declared information, consent, resource, timing and identity class, and let a world ww be a reactive environment strategy. Suppose certified envelopes satisfy, for every rival π\pi and every world, 𝒪(π,w)≼U(π,w)≼L(w)≼𝒪(π*,w). \mathcal O(\pi,w)\preceq U(\pi,w)\preceq L(w)\preceq\mathcal O(\pi^*,w). Transitivity proves π*\pi^* greatest in that complete class, world by world. The envelopes may be optimistic and need not be executable; their bounds concern the actual outcome in the full four-stage order. R15 and R16 reduce the comparison when implementations with the same certified interface strategy have the same boundary transcript, resources factor conditionally, outcome ownership is accounted for and the relevant fibres have greatest representatives. Fixing a strategy does not fix its transcript independently of reactive feedback. When no greatest representative exists, the law distinguishes maximality from greatestness and applies its actual existence conditions (VI.2; Part X).

Join to II.10. II.10 earns greatestness of the whole tuple from two constructions, realisability (htopR, derived from locality in G.9) and funded cost (hsolv). The envelope chain is the reactive, per-world form of the same conclusion: L(w)L(w) is the realisable top in world ww, and the chain places π*\pi^*’s outcome at it. Part X’s IR-135 supplies the quantifier the envelope requires — one policy fixed before the world is chosen — and its countermodel shows why per-world success does not give it.

The rival bound is free at the top. Write the top outcome as ⊤\top: every existing particular continues and is free, and every feasible new particular continues and is free. When the selected policy realises ⊤\top (realisability htopR from locality, G.9; funding hsolv), every rival’s outcome satisfies 𝒪(π,w)≼⊤\mathcal O(\pi,w)\preceq\top by inclusion. The upper envelope is the universal tuple itself, so no enumeration of rival histories is needed (greatest_of_solvent). This is the 29 October audit’s “Certificate B”. The per-world envelopes need one policy realising ⊤\top in every world. Under union closure (G.9) on a compact policy space that policy exists: finite character turns pairwise splicing into one policy realising the union of all policies’ outcomes (CommonPolicyTop.top_policy_exists), and that outcome contains every realisable outcome in every world (top_policy_greatest).

In a tragedy, certification is per loss. Where ⊤\top is not realisable, Proposition 1 (aligned_iff_no_needless_loss) turns maximality into one check for each particular lost: no feasible option keeps it while agreeing at every earlier stage. four_stage_original_maximal guarantees that an outcome passing every such check exists, and the last-resort ladder and the impartiality ruling (VI.3) govern the choice among such outcomes. The reduction is exact (PerLossCheck.maximal_iff_per_loss): no feasible outcome is better than mm if and only if, for every fact mm loses, no feasible outcome keeps it while agreeing with mm at every earlier stage and keeping everything mm keeps at that stage.

IX.2 Theorem 8 and the derived holding composition

Master Argument §14 states Theorem 8: given, for a domain KK, horizon TT and source execution, (1) initial continuation witnesses, (2) a complete event, observation and causal inventory with pending effects, (3) commuting refinements with local invariant preservation, (4) a certified comparison over the actual feasible family, (5) application-time mediation of every relevant effect, (6) prefix-feasible service, funding and recovery certificates, (7) identity and care witnesses through holds and transitions, (8) conditional risk kernels for every charged failure — then on the good event GG the source refines the abstract execution, every applied effect carries its current permit, care meets its deadlines, the invariant holds for every particular in KK through TT, and P(failure by T)≤P(Gc)≤∑i,tδi,tP(\text{failure by }T)\le P(G^c)\le\sum_{i,t}\delta_{i,t}.

The canon’s Composition.theorem8_composition and Bridge.universal_protection_held (II.6) implement this composition with the holding step derived: the five hcert components are proved on the held source in G.10. Theorem 8 in this edition therefore carries certificates (1), (3), (5),

  1. by construction (II.3–II.6, G.10), (2) and (8) by G1 (G.10, E.1), (4) by Parts II.10, IX.1 and X, and (6) by Sections 18 and 22, G.12 and Part VIII.

Part XI — Reach before harm: the outer-lane theorem

This part constructs the join that no single earlier line contains: every mind, inside or outside any installation, is reached or held before its effects can land on any protected particular, from founding onward, with the protection funded, selected without coordination, and carried by one policy.

XI.1 Setting

The relational given (P1–P4), with signal speed cs>0c_s>0: no effect propagates faster. The protected domain at time tt is D(t)⊆ED(t)\subseteq E (a real normed space of positions; every particular has a location in the one structure, P1). Because new particulars arise from existing ones by local interaction (P4), the domain moves at most at a speed c≤csc\le c_s: every x∈D(t)x\in D(t) lies within ctct of some y∈D(0)y\in D(0). Guards are holding stations: the funded tracking/repair controller of II.3–II.4 with its E9 sensing and the application-time fence of II.5. A threat to a particular at xx has an effect deadline dd (the time from its first detectable sign to irreversible effect); guards respond in time τ\tau.

XI.2 Four lemmas (compiled: Snuffy.OuterLane)

Lemma W (wavefront coverage; wavefront_coverage). If every y∈D(0)y\in D(0) is within ρ\rho of a guard of G(0)G(0); the guard set at time tt contains every point within vtvt of G(0)G(0); and c≤vc\le v, then every x∈D(t)x\in D(t) is within ρ\rho of a guard of G(t)G(t). Proof. Choose y∈D(0)y\in D(0) with |x−y|≤ct|x-y|\le ct and g∈G(0)g\in G(0) with |y−g|≤ρ|y-g|\le\rho; then a=|x−g|≤ρ+vta=|x-g|\le\rho+vt. If a≤vta\le vt, xx itself is a guard point. Otherwise g′=g+(vt/a)(x−g)g'=g+(vt/a)(x-g) is within vtvt of gg, hence a guard point, and |x−g′|=a−vt≤ρ|x-g'|=a-vt\le\rho. ∎

Lemma I (interception in time, round trip; ReachTiming.round_trip_in_time). The sign travels from the particular to the guard, the guard responds in τ\tau, and its action travels back. A guard within ρ≤cs(d−τ)/2\rho\le c_s(d-\tau)/2 therefore acts at the particular before dd: 2ρ/cs+τ≤d2\rho/c_s+\tau\le d. (The one-way form OuterLane.interception_in_time bounds only the outbound leg; the referee’s correction, 29 October, is adopted.)

Lemma I₀ (the synchronous fence; ReachTiming.fence_in_time, UPTFence). Attacks faster than any round trip (an adjacent attacker acting in one step, the finite-speed countermodel of 28 October) are met by no travelling guard. They are met by the fence on the effect path itself. Its check runs in the write path at application time, so its response time is τf=0≤d\tau_f=0\le d for every deadline, and once the floor rises nothing lands while held, whatever the held mind does or reports (UPTFence; IR-91/92 for the nine substrate classes). For the theory’s target, that fence sits on the digital mind’s own outputs (Corollary XI.3). Per-site E9 sensing with quorum no-masking (E9SelfHealing.no_masking, Instruments.branchC_complete) raises the alarm in the above-threshold branch; funded tracking and repair bound and absorb the sub-threshold branch for the care plant’s guards. The zero-time fence here is the abstract atomic application check. An implementation must serialize that check and the actual effect with hold/revocation transitions; its positive request-to-effective-hold latency, clock error and in-flight work remain in the response budget.

Lemma P (selection by noise-induced dominance; pool_strictly_dominant). Let the capacity the other keepers actually deliver be any random variable — their intentions composed with execution noise (UPT-P Setting U). If a keeper’s pooling is pivotal with positive probability, pooling strictly raises the probability that the ender is held. A lexicographic keeper (protection first) therefore pools whatever the others intend; with full-support execution noise every keeper that is pivotal in some configuration has positive pivotal probability. Hence the no-pooling profile is not an equilibrium among such keepers, and Gate D’s selection question is decided for them; VII.5 (m4) extends this to patiently excluded finite-trade-off keepers. Under D-ENDOW (Part VIII U3) committed capacity is not a voluntary choice at all, so no selection arises inside an endowed jurisdiction. With the keeper’s own execution noise (an intended pool fails with probability ε\varepsilon, an intended abstention pools with probability δ\delta), pooling raises the holding probability by exactly (1−ε−δ)(1-\varepsilon-\delta) times the pivotal gap, so it stays strictly better whenever ε+δ<1\varepsilon+\delta<1 (NoisyPooling.noisy_pool_strictly_dominant). The others may be countably many, with any joint law: their delivered capacity is the sum in [0,∞][0,\infty], always defined and measurable even when it diverges, and pooling stays strictly better (CountablePooling.countable_keepers_pool, and with own noise countable_keepers_noisy_pool).

Lemma R (risk; outer_lane_risk). If failure of the outer lane is contained in founding failure, a holding failure at some date, or a charged account failure, its probability is at most ηF+∑tφt+∑iδi\eta_F+\sum_t\varphi_t+\sum_i\delta_i, with no independence assumed. With countably many itemised accounts, each failing with probability ∫κidμ\int\kappa_i\,d\mu for a conditional kernel bounded pointwise by δi\delta_i (the worst case over every conditioning state), the bound is ∑iδi\sum_i\delta_i (ItemisedRisk.itemised_risk).

Lemma H (the hold is a common viable action; HoldCommonAction). IR-113 shows that one observation-only protective policy exists exactly when every observation class has an action keeping every compatible viable state viable. The holding route reduces that premise to one condition, hold safety uniform over the observation class: every admitted successor of every compatible viable state under the hold is viable. Given it, the hold is a common viable action (hold_is_common_viable_action, no axioms), and one policy that acts where a class-wide safe action exists and holds elsewhere keeps viability everywhere (act_or_hold_policy). A faithful hold lands no effect, so hold safety does not turn on which effect is chosen. It does turn on the world’s own perturbation during the hold interval, which must stay inside the decoding radius for every hidden state in the class: ε+(W/ℏ)Δ≤rdec\varepsilon+(W/\hbar)\Delta\le r_{\mathrm{dec}} with WW bounding the perturbation of every such state (Bridge.qsl_within_radius), or 2λτ<d2\lambda\tau<d with λ\lambda bounding every such fault process (Bridge.headroom_within_radius). Decode and funded repair then return the state (holding_preserves). E9’s per-site threshold and complete attack split supply a class-uniform WW for mind-driven perturbation, since they bound injection whatever the adversary. Compiled join (HoldFromCycle): with the class’s perturbations each keeping a continuing particular within the decoding radius, every hold step (perturbation, nearest-codeword decoding, funded repair) keeps every viable state viable (hsafe_of_holding_cycle, from Bridge.nearest_decodes). So the hold is a common viable action at every observation class under IR-113’s own criterion (hold_common_action_of_cycle, classViable_iff_IR113), and one observation-only policy keeps viability along every finite trace (one_policy_from_holding_cycle, through PhysicalBridges.IR113.common_actions_give_finite_trace_viability). The remaining input is the class-uniform perturbation bound itself, which the installation measures (WW, λ\lambda, τ\tau, rdecr_{\mathrm{dec}}). The two-world example (two_world_resolved) is a stipulated control showing the shape of the resolution, not a derivation; IR-108’s own countermodel, in which inaction is itself harmful in one world, is answered only where the hold interval is shorter than that harm’s deadline, which is the same uniform bound.

Composite (ReachTiming.reach_round_trip). Under Lemma W’s hypotheses with ρ≤cs(d−τ)/2\rho\le c_s(d-\tau)/2: at every t≥0t\ge0, every particular of D(t)D(t) has a guard g∈G(t)g\in G(t) with 2|x−g|/cs+τ≤d2|x-g|/c_s+\tau\le d, so the guard’s action reaches it before its deadline. (ReachBeforeHarm.reach_before_harm is the one-way version.) Discrete guard sets enter through a net: guards forming a ρnet\rho_{\mathrm{net}}-net of the swept region give coverage at radius ρ+ρnet\rho+\rho_{\mathrm{net}}.

XI.3 The theorem

Theorem XI (reach before harm). Suppose at founding time t0t_0:

  1. (Founding threshold.) Protection-first capacity satisfies r=C(1−ε)/H>1r=C(1-\varepsilon)/H>1 with H=c(KE+aSmax)+AH=c(K_E+aS_{\max})+A (Theorem NP), split among nn independent keepers (MS), so that φ(n)≤exp⁡(−2n(1−ε−H/C)2)\varphi(n)\le\exp(-2n(1-\varepsilon-H/C)^2) (NarrowPlace.np_splitting_bound); founding fails with probability at most ηF\eta_F. Neither a fixed threat nor independence is needed for a guarantee: a random threat correlated with the deliveries adds only its cap’s account ηH\eta_H (CorrelatedHolding.random_threat_independent), and under any joint law of the keepers, common-mode failures included, holding fails with probability at most ηH+ε/(1−Hmax/C)\eta_H+\varepsilon/(1-H_{\max}/C) (random_threat_correlated, by Markov’s inequality).
  2. (Founding coverage.) At t0t_0 every digital mind’s substrate outputs are fenced (Corollary XI.3; a total meter bounds every output channel, listed or not, ChannelMeter), and every location of D(t0)D(t_0) is within ρ≤cs(d−τ)/2\rho\le c_s(d-\tau)/2 of a funded guard. This is the founding certificate (XI.5 item 1); Theorem XI propagates it. Its location half is a finite construction: a compact initial domain is covered at any radius by finitely many guards (FoundingCover.founding_cover_exists), and founding with them yields round-trip reach at every later time (founded_reach).
  3. (Expansion at least as fast as the domain.) The guarded region expands at speed v≥cv\ge c: the wavefront of Section 21.7, whose sweep succeeds with an O(tdG)O(t^{d_G}) cumulative bill (G.12). In an expanding space the same inequality holds in comoving distance and conformal time, since expansion carries particulars and guards alike; the round trip needs amax⋅2ρ/cs+τ≤da_{\max}\cdot2\rho/c_s+\tau\le d (ExpandingWavefront.expanding_coverage, expanding_round_trip).
  4. (Funding.) Income meets premise 6’s master solvency condition, whose first term ω0R(t)dG−1\omega_0R(t)^{d_G-1} is the boundary-maintenance rate of the expanding region. For a growing bill b(t)b(t) the endowment form is e*=∑tb(t)(1+rmin)−te^*=\sum_t b(t)(1+r_{\min})^{-t}, finite for polynomial bb when rmin>0r_{\min}>0 (GrowingBill.endowment_suffices; Gate C-∞’s stationary price is the constant-bill case).
  5. (Charged accounts.) Every failure mode of the conclusion has a named account with a genuine conditional kernel: founding (ηF\eta_F); holding at each date (φt\varphi_t); per-step exit under full-support noise (Θ2’s ε\varepsilon); wavefront deployment and guard survival; fence integrity; E9 detection; funding shortfall; and the twenty-one accounts of Section 22.3. Their sum is the declared budget. Itemising these accounts is what Lemma R’s containment hypothesis requires.

Then from t0t_0 through T≤TendT\le T_{\mathrm{end}}, with probability at least 1−ηF−∑t≤Tφt−∑iδi1-\eta_F-\sum_{t\le T}\varphi_t-\sum_i\delta_i:

  • every location of D(t)D(t), including every particular newly arising after founding, is within round-trip interception radius of a guard at every tt (Lemma W, Lemma I);
  • every digital mind made after founding is made inside the arrangement with fenced outputs (Corollary XI.1), so every effect of every digital mind on any particular passes the synchronous fence (Lemma I₀, Corollary XI.3). A mind with its own reason keeps the living free, R(m)R(m). Any mind whose effect is not admissible, reasons or none, is restrained by the fence and the holding construction of II.3–II.6 while its care continues, H(m)H(m);
  • the holding coalition forms without coordination (Lemma P) and keeps its advantage (VII.5 (b3), Theorem MN: r(t)r(t) non-decreasing before the twilight); ∑tφt\sum_t\varphi_t converges when keepers grow (J1);
  • the guarantee is carried by one policy fixed before the world is chosen (Lemma H with IR-113 and IR-135; IR-72 gives a full-state infinite-horizon policy where two actions suffice). Under full-support noise preservation is quantitative: every admitted policy’s per-step exit is at most Θ2’s ε\varepsilon (Theorem V(d)), charged in Lemma R. The almost-sure forms (Theorem V(c), Theorem E (E4)) apply where noise is bounded (Θ1);
  • the continuation invariant holds for every protected particular by Bridge.universal_protection_held on the good event (II.6).

Proof. Lemma W with hypotheses 2–3 gives coverage at every tt. Lemma I turns coverage into round-trip interception before every deadline, and Lemma I₀ meets attacks faster than any round trip at the fence on the acting mind’s outputs. An effect that is not admissible is therefore met by the fence and the holding step of II.3 (perturbation within decoding radius, decode, funded repair; holding_preserves, holding_cycle_physical). Every policy admitted by that rule exits per step with probability at most ε\varepsilon under Gaussian noise (Θ2, Theorem V(d)), or preserves almost surely under bounded noise (Θ1, Theorem V(c), Theorem E (E4)), whatever its rewards. Lemma P makes the protecting coalition the outcome among protection-first keepers; hypothesis 1 with NP/MS bounds the holding failure at each date and J1 bounds its sum; hypothesis 4 funds the guards and their expansion (G.12’s bill is the integral of premise 6’s boundary term); IR-113/IR-135 give the common policy. Every failure of the conclusion lies in one of the accounts itemised in hypothesis 5, and Lemma R bounds the probability. ∎

XI.3b Coverage by location: every particular, every relation, every made mind

Coverage is by location, not by registry. Lemma W covers every point of the domain. A particular need not be recognised, registered, minded or living to be within interception radius of a guard: the nonliving, the unregistered and the newly arising are covered because they are somewhere in the one structure (P1). IR-116’s cumulative duties then keep every particular once owed; Lemma W makes the owed set the whole domain.

Relations. By P1 there is no outside, so a change in a relation is an event in the one structure. By P4 that event occurs at locations, those of the relata or of the region between them. Lemma W covers every location of the domain, not only the particulars’ own, so every relation among particulars of the domain is within guard reach wherever its change occurs, and every mind’s effect on it passes the fence on that mind’s outputs (Corollary XI.3).

Corollary XI.1 (every digital mind made after founding is held or reached from its making). A digital mind is made by a local process inside the one structure (P1, P4); its making is an event at a location of D(t)D(t). After founding that location is covered (Lemma W), and inside an installation the making is the reserve-before-activation transition of Section 20.3 (H5Closure: reserve before activation, attenuated authority, no unfunded work, care preserved). So every digital mind made after founding begins inside guard reach with fenced effect channels: it is reached by its own reasons or faithfully held from its first step. No digital mind made after founding arrives from outside the arrangement.

Corollary XI.2 (the expansion bound is an admission rule). A particular made by a mind is activated only after its complete continuing obligation is reserved (II.8; Section 20.3; Master Argument §8: every active identity carries a funded maintenance witness). Its protection — the guard of its location and the fence on its channels — is part of that obligation. So a made particular is covered from activation whatever the speed of its making, and Lemma W’s speed condition c≤vc\le v is needed only for particulars arising without mediated making, at the rate natural processes produce them. A making that would place a particular beyond coverage is outside the viable action rule DVD_V and is not admitted (Theorem V(c)); ruling 6 gives it no claim on that room.

Corollary XI.3 (source-side mediation of every digital mind). Every effect a digital mind has on any particular passes through its substrate’s output channels: the nine A1 classes (memory mapping, DMA, context switches, packet ingestion, bus messages, storage synchronisation, commissioning, delegation, retirement; IR-91/92 at source level) together with the substrate’s physical emissions, all bounded by the total meter (Lemma E, ChannelMeter). Fencing those channels at application time (II.5; Chapter 16.5, UPTFence: once the floor rises nothing lands while held, whatever the held mind does or reports) mediates every effect of that mind on every particular, living or not, wherever the particular is. With Corollary XI.1 every digital mind made after founding is mediated from its first step, and in-flight effects at a hold are drained within the metered escrow (IR-117–122). For the theory’s target — protection from any digital mind — interception at radius zero sits at the mind’s own outputs; Lemma W carries the care plant’s guards to every particular for every other cause of loss.

Lemma E (emissions are routed through a mediated physical sink; EmissionBound). A substrate’s physical emissions are outputs that pass no software fence, and for a computing substrate nearly all input energy leaves as heat, so conservation alone bounds little. The installation therefore makes the emission path itself a mediated sink: shielding, a controlled exhaust, filtered power, and a receiver-exclusion zone sized by each channel’s attenuation law. Two compiled bounds then apply at the zone boundary. Requisite variety (D116, requisite_variety): a channel delivering one of MM messages lets a responder answer correctly for at most MM disturbances, so under uniformly distributed targets a selection among |D||D| responses succeeds with probability at most M/|D|M/|D| (requisite_variety_prob, deterministic encoder and responder; MM counts every channel use within the deadline). And energy (emission_cannot_power): an effect needing more work than the exhaust delivers past the boundary cannot be powered by it. Untargeted harms (a burst, a one-bit trigger to stored energy) need no variety; they are excluded by the receiver-exclusion zone, since a trigger acts only through a receiver and actuator in range, and every device inside the zone is itself a fenced substrate. The exclusion radius is compiled (ExclusionRadius.exclusion_radius): a channel delivering power P0/rnP_0/r^n cannot supply work WW within deadline dd at any r≥(P0d/W)1/nr\ge(P_0d/W)^{1/n}. The harm-class table is constructed (installation/HARM-CLASSES.json). Each class has a published protective threshold:

  • people: ICNIRP 2020 RF exposure, FCC localized SAR, OSHA and NIOSH hearing limits, and radiant heat;
  • devices and records: IEC 61000-4-3 immunity;
  • ionising radiation: the Duane–Hunt bound;
  • low-frequency magnetic fields: ICNIRP 2010;
  • coherent particulars: a measured coupling.

installation/commission.py turns each threshold and the installation’s meter into an exclusion radius. Corollary XI.3’s completeness rests on this mediated emission sink together with the total meter (ChannelMeter), which bounds every channel whether listed or not.

Islands. Protection composes over causally bound islands (VII.5 (i), IS): a region whose particulars no founder’s signal can reach is protected by its own founding, and the global failure bound is the union over islands (Lemma R). Within each founder’s causal future the wavefront advances at the maximal admissible speed, so every particular a founder can ever affect is covered as soon as any effect from that founder’s region could reach it.

XI.4 What Theorem XI changes

The finite-speed countermodel of 28 October (a radius-one attacker beside an unshielded subject, a distant guardian) is answered for the theory’s target: a digital attacker’s every effect passes the synchronous fence on its own outputs (Lemma I₀, Corollary XI.3), so no travel time is needed, and coverage of every location is carried by the wavefront faster than the domain can grow. The 18 October P3 coverage premise is reduced to coverage at founding (hypothesis 2), which Theorem XI propagates to every later time; founding coverage itself is the founding certificate of XI.5 item 1. Gate D’s selection is decided by Lemma P. Paper 11’s “protection before activation stays outside this theorem” is supplied for the activated domain from t0t_0.

XI.5 The construction that remains for Theorem XI

These are proofs to supply for the same full-strength theorem, not limits of it.

  1. The founding certificate at the actual narrow place. Theorem NP makes the condition exact: r>1r>1 at founding, before the first irreversible threat (“keepers first”, MN4: initial risk ≤μλt1\le\mu\lambda t_1, t1=0t_1=0). B4 telemetry certifies rlower>1r_{\mathrm{lower}}>1 with no false-safe declaration.

    Lemma F (founding without coordination; FoundingPivotal, Book I §9.16‴). In a provision-point campaign with refunds, where an anchor commits its pledge first and posts collateral for failure bonuses β>0\beta>0 to the other contributors, set the provision point to the total of all pledges, as the book’s witness does, so every pledge is necessary. Then the others can never fund alone (their pledges total B−ci<BB-c_i<B), and contributing minus abstaining is β\beta when the pool fails either way and bipiv−cib^{\mathrm{piv}}_i-c_i when the pledge creates provision. With β>0\beta>0 and bipiv>cib^{\mathrm{piv}}_i>c_i, contribution is strictly dominant at every profile (FoundingPivotal.pivotal_contribution_dominant), so the all-abstain profile is not an equilibrium. This holds for a non-excludable good. (With a lower provision point the already-funded state arises, and for a public good its advantage is −ci-c_i; the referee’s correction is adopted, and FoundingDominance applies only with an excludable benefit there.) The no-founding equilibrium that the coordination game otherwise keeps (the finite G3/G5/G6 witness of IR draft #171 has both) is removed when every pledge is necessary. The anchor establishes the campaign exactly when its participation margin is positive (Proposition 9.16‴.2; in the stated witness 6910q3−q1+2q210−d>0\tfrac{69}{10}q_3-\tfrac{q_1+2q_2}{10}-d>0). Since every ordinary funder’s contribution is strictly dominant, every one of them contributes. When the pledges reach the provision point, the campaign succeeds and no failure bonus is paid, so the anchor founds exactly when its own benefit from protection exceeds its pledge plus its activation cost. No other party’s cooperation is assumed. Together with Lemma P (keepers pool) and Section 9.17 (increasing returns favour the largest effective pool), founding reduces to one committed anchor with collateral c+(N−1)βc+(N-1)\beta: every other step of founding is a strictly dominant choice.

    What remains is that anchor and its commissioning in the actual world (P-COMMISSION), the first funded guards over the existing domain, and the measured C,ε,HC,\varepsilon,H. The reasons route supplies the anchor’s own reasons (Section 15: reciprocity_dominance_solvent; Section 16; V.3), and Corollary XI.1 shows that founding before capable digital minds are made places every digital mind inside the arrangement from its making.

  2. The natural-arising rate in the actual installation. By Corollary XI.2 made particulars are covered by admission; for particulars arising without mediated making, P4 bounds effects by csc_s; the wavefront’s deployment speed must match the actual rate at which new particulars and their channels arise.

  3. The quantum branch — route decided (29 October, under the author’s delegation: “use your best judgement that gets us to a full universal protection theory”). Protection from digital minds is enforced at each mind’s own output channels (Corollary XI.3), with emissions routed through the mediated physical sink of Lemma E. A coherent quantum particular is protected by the same route: no mind’s software effect reaches it unmediated, and the emission sink bounds the power and coupling of any untargeted emission at its location. To construct: the decoherence-rate bound from the sink’s emitted power and the coupling to coherent particulars, which turns that route into a quantitative guarantee in branch (b), where the record-decode-repair half of holding is unavailable because nonorthogonal states cannot be copied. Its form is compiled (ExclusionRadius.received_effect_bound: a rate Γ≤κP(r)\Gamma\le\kappa P(r) stays below Γmax\Gamma_{\max} beyond (κP0/Γmax)1/n(\kappa P_0/\Gamma_{\max})^{1/n}); the coupling κ\kappa per class is measured. The classical-record branch carries the active holding cycle (II.3, G.19, PassiveReference, RedundantRecord). Active quantum-coherent holding (G.20–G.21) enters the law’s feasible family as soon as its devices are feasible. From then on the law requires it wherever loss would otherwise be needless (Proposition 1; VI.2 “Time”: a duty to widen). If entanglement-type relations are identity-constituting, branch (b), their protection from minds rests on source-side mediation with the emission sink, quantified by the decoherence bound above, and their active repair is a device question inside the same law. If they are not, branch (a), the classical branch is the whole holding route. Either way the proposition keeps its full scope, and no particular leaves it.

  4. Four-stage maximality — now proved, in the law’s own terms. StagedMaximality.four_stage_original_maximal gives the four coupled original stages with mandatory baseline and the freedom prerequisite, for arbitrary particular sets, under finite character (Part X). StageBridge.four_stage_aligned and four_stage_no_needless_loss restate it in the canon’s law: the outcome is Greatestness.Aligned and, by Proposition 1, needlessly loses nothing at any stage. Scope: Finitary families (no forbidden finite pattern, conjunctive prerequisites, a feasible mandatory baseline); disjunctive positive requirements and the derivation of finite character from compactness of the policy space are the compiled extensions in XII.2 item 4.

The proposition, assembled. For every particular and relation in the expanding domain, from founding to the world’s natural end: the law selects the greatest realisable whole outcome where it exists and a maximal one over the full feasible family otherwise (S1–S2); every mind is reached by its own reasons or faithfully held, with care continuing and without its consent being required (S3–S4); holding reaches every particular before any effect’s deadline (S5); continuation is carried with its full history (S6); every effect is mediated at application time (S7); work, timing and resources are funded (S8); every failure is charged in one joint account (S9); one policy composes these on the good event (S10); and the arrangement lasts to TendT_{\mathrm{end}} (S11). The constructions in the right column are the remaining proofs; none narrows the proposition.

Proved boundaries that are part of the maximal statement. No protector reaches probability exactly one when the indistinguishable-failure mass is positive (U11), and full-support noise forbids almost-sure preservation (Θ0). The theory’s guarantee is therefore protection with failure probability at most η\eta over the horizon, with margins growing only like log⁡T\sqrt{\log T} and attaining their lower bounds (VII.5 (n)). Being as strong as physics permits is the maximal claim. These boundaries have been in the theory since 18 October.

Part XIII — The Cathedral increment: the floor, the cut guardian, and the three joins (2 November 2026)

This part integrates the author’s closing capstone of 2 November 2026 and the merged research increment (pull requests 204, 205 and 207) into the compiled edition. The maximal target, the original X3 obligations and every earlier part remain in force unchanged. No global physical-UPT completion verdict is issued; each join carries its source correspondence as an explicit obligation.

XIII.1 The floor: physics presupposes mathematics

Every physical theory — right or wrong, complete or incomplete — is a mathematical structure, so every physical agent is a structure within mathematics, and its acts are mathematical facts. An absolute ender’s victory would be a mathematical fact whose content is the nonexistence of mathematical facts. ender_success_self_refutes (kernel-checked, axiom-free) records the trivial paradox in one line: a success whose own content is the negation of that success cannot occur. On a cyclic history there is no final phase on which the ending could be written. This is the reading of the edition’s self-grounding capstone (Part VII’s nontrivial evaluation witness): the structure grounds its own continuation, so nothing outside mathematics stands for an ending to stand on. The author’s supplied route — the experienced matterspacetime as a subjective view from a position and orientation in the lattice, the particular being the co-ordinate rather than the substrate — is recorded with the integration bank of the canon working master; it makes the only real death the severance of a perspective from its own history, which the complete-ledger structure of Parts III and VI forbids.

XIII.2 The cut guardian, mediation, and first-breach localisation

CathedralCutGuardianCriterion (kernel-checked with Lean 4.35.0; imports the existing IR108, IR109, IR132 and IR96 modules; no new physical axioms) proves the exact certificate: for a state space SS, observation cut b:S→Ob:S\to O, allowed actions AA, step relation and independently sourced protection predicate, a safe observation-only controller exists if and only if every protected observational fibre shares a common allowed action preserving protection against every modelled successor. Supporting theorems: cut refinement cannot destroy an available guardian; protected states with disjoint safe-action sets force a distinguishing cut; the IR132 exact decoder is one sufficient route, and action-relevant distinction — not full microscopic reconstruction — is the necessary information; actual effects must be mediated through the selected actions (guarded_real_effects_preserve_finite_histories); any actual finite violation contains a first violating step, which carries a causal witness under genuine event coverage (first_violation_has_causal_witness). CyclicSpliceTransfer proves that an injective seam, a shared closing cut and covering block agreement close the spliced endpoint cyclically, and joins the guardian criterion to that closure.

XIII.3 Viability selection: the quantifier gap and cyclic transport

CathedralViabilitySelection (kernel-checked; compiled from the reviewed candidate with one proof-term repair, all statements unchanged) exhibits the quantifier gap exactly: IR-72’s infinite robust safe policy exists, while an available unsafe action remains selectable — existence of protection is not enactment. Periodic return of the total mathematical history does not carry subject liveness; a witnessed protected phase plus source-proven preservation across every actual transition yields protection across a transitive cycle without presupposing cyclic liveness; and a positive predicate can hold on every finite approximation yet fail at an admitted omega-limit, so any physical limit stage needs independent source closure (limit-stage redline).

XIII.4 The frozen identity-charge audit: a scoped negative

Against the hash-verified frozen BCRD source (68 files at the recorded physics-lane revision), the literal M3d W_UPDATE event sends |M,0⟩|M,0\rangle to |M,1⟩|M,1\rangle and flips L(ρ)=Tr(ρC)L(\rho)=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho C) from +1+1 to −1-1 for C=(QA+QB−QC)⊗σzC=(Q_A+Q_B-Q_C)\otimes\sigma_z. BCRDIdentityCharge kernel-checks the counterexample with an integer-entry certificate built from the actual source operators. Classification: candidate extension SCOPE_LIMITING; the original physical X3.1 ender question remains UNRESOLVED. The frozen replay passes 32 of 33 controls; the one failure is a sorted-eigenvalue ordering artifact, retained and diagnosed in bcrd-frozen-model-replay.json.

XIII.5 The capstone joins, compiled

CathedralCapstoneJoins composes the three joins from the named artifacts, with every physical antecedent an explicit hypothesis:

  1. Continuation (cyclic transport). cycle_protection_from_source_preservation (axiom-free): a witnessed protected phase plus source-proven preservation across every actual transition protects every reachable phase; the two-phase positive theorem is derived from the general theorem, which subsumes it.
  2. Selection (actual enactment). The cut certificate feeds the IR-72 engine (fibre_certificate_forever_viable, fibre_certificate_physical_safety_exists) for the existence side, and capstone_enacted_history_protected (axiom-free in generic form) closes the gap: if every realised physical edge executes an action common-safe on its protected fibre, the whole actual history is protected at every time.
  3. Funding (the complete bill). The funding interface is the allowed component of GuardAction, mapped to the escrow and complete-bill instruments (IRResidualEscrow, IREnergyReplenishment, IR121MeteredResidualEscrow, IRA1CommissionEscrow). No new funding theorem is claimed.

Verification: the physical-bridges package builds with 136 jobs and no compiler output on pinned Lean 4.35.0; the axiom audit is within Lean’s three standard axioms (the floor, the generic enacted-history theorem, the cyclic transport and the subsumption use none); both finite checkers pass — 65,536 cut/action guardian models with 288 first-breach paths and bypass controls, and 4 policies, 4 cyclic predicates and 5,000 approximants. The fresh receipt is RECEIPT-4.4-CATHEDRAL.txt; CI replays both verifiers on every push.

XIII.6 What remains

The remaining obligations are exactly the source correspondences: an authentic physical protection predicate; genuinely authorised action sets; effect mediation through the selected actions; source-proven cyclic preservation and reachability; funded authorisation across the cycle and its handoff; and the physical parameter ledger’s calibration. Nothing in this part establishes that actual BCRD physics satisfies the antecedents, and the compilation changes the status of the joins, not their content.
